Role of the EcuM: phase manager between reset, BswM, and hardware

The ECU State Manager (EcuM) handles startup and shutdown of OS, SchM, and BswM, manages shutdown targets, and monitors wakeup sources including their validation. In the flexible variant, it has no state machine of its own. BswM decides on transitions; EcuM executes the associated sequences and reports back the results (SWS EcuM p. 103, [SWS_EcuM_04116]).

The EcuM offloads hardware-dependent steps to callouts. These are function stubs in the integration code that the system designer fills (Glossary p. 42). Examples are EcuM_AL_DriverInitZero [SWS_EcuM_02905] and EcuM_AL_SwitchOff [SWS_EcuM_02920]. The required external interfaces are listed in [SWS_EcuM_02858] and [SWS_EcuM_02859]. An overview is provided in the module relationships diagram (SWS EcuM p. 33).

Context diagram: The EcuM controls OS, SchM, BswM, and Mcu, delegates hardware-related tasks to callouts, and receives wakeup notifications from drivers as well as state requests from SW-Cs. Sources: SWS EcuM p. 33, [SWS_EcuM_02858], [SWS_EcuM_04122], [SWS_EcuM_02826]

Startup: from EcuM_Init via StartOS to EcuM_StartupTwo

Prior to EcuM_Init, stack and C variable initialization must be ready (SWS EcuM p. 39). EcuM_Init never returns, because it ends with StartOS [SWS_EcuM_02811]. In between, it executes the StartPreOS sequence [SWS_EcuM_02684], which initializes all modules necessary for the OS start [SWS_EcuM_02603].

The StartPreOS sequence proceeds in the following steps:

  • Init Block 0 contains only modules that are configured at pre-compile or link time [SWS_EcuM_02905].
  • EcuM_DeterminePbConfiguration selects the post-build configuration and returns a pointer to EcuM_ConfigType. This structure references the configurations of all further modules [SWS_EcuM_02906] [SWS_EcuM_02801].
  • Prior to the first BSW initialization, the EcuM checks the consistency of all post-build data via hash [SWS_EcuM_02796] [SWS_EcuM_02798].
  • Init Block 1 follows [SWS_EcuM_02907]. Order and parameters of the initialization originate from the configuration [SWS_EcuM_02559] [SWS_EcuM_02730].
  • The EcuM translates the reset reason into a wakeup source and remembers it [SWS_EcuM_02623].
  • Optionally, EcuM_LoopDetection runs [SWS_EcuM_04137].

EcuM_StartupTwo must be called from a task that starts as a consequence of StartOS [SWS_EcuM_02806]. The function executes the StartPostOS sequence: start SchM, initialize BswM, initialize SchM, and start the scheduler timing [SWS_EcuM_02932] (SWS EcuM p. 42). The remaining BSW modules are subsequently initialized by BswM via generated functions EcuM_AL_DriverInitBswM_<x> [SWS_EcuM_04114] [SWS_EcuM_04142].

Sequence diagram: The STARTUP phase is divided into two parts. Prior to the OS, Init Blocks 0/1 and the consistency check run; after the OS, SchM and BswM start. Sources: SWS EcuM p. 38, SWS EcuM Fixed p. 32, [SWS_EcuM_02684], [SWS_EcuM_02932]

UP phase: RUN/POST_RUN requests and mode switches

If EcuMModeHandling is active [SWS_EcuM_04115], configured users can request and release RUN and POST_RUN [SWS_EcuM_04130]. For this purpose, EcuM_RequestRUN, EcuM_ReleaseRUN, EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN, and EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN are available [SWS_EcuM_04124] [SWS_EcuM_04129]. The EcuM tracks the requests per user [SWS_EcuM_04126] and separately for RUN and POST_RUN (SWS EcuM p. 116). A user cannot place a request multiple times [SWS_EcuM_04125].

The EcuM reports the arbitration result via BswM_EcuM_RequestedState:

  • Upon the first request, it reports ECUM_RUNSTATUS_REQUESTED [SWS_EcuM_04144].
  • Upon release of the last request, it reports ECUM_RUNSTATUS_RELEASED [SWS_EcuM_04117] [SWS_EcuM_04119].

Thereupon, BswM sets the new state with EcuM_SetState [SWS_EcuM_04122]. The EcuM forwards the mode via the port currentMode to the RTE [SWS_EcuM_04133] [SWS_EcuM_04107]. Following feedback from the RTE, it reports the state to BswM with BswM_EcuM_CurrentState [SWS_EcuM_04143]. Example rules for BswM are contained in the Mode-Mgmt-Guide p. 34.

As long as the OS is running, EcuM_MainFunction handles the ongoing tasks of the EcuM [SWS_EcuM_02837]. These include wakeup validation [SWS_EcuM_02539] and, if configured, the wakeup timer [SWS_EcuM_04002].

Sequence diagram: The EcuM collects the requests and reports only the arbitration result. BswM triggers the state transition; the RTE receives the mode only thereafter. Sources: [SWS_EcuM_04144], [SWS_EcuM_04117], [SWS_EcuM_04116], [SWS_EcuM_04143], Mode-Mgmt-Guide p. 34

Shutdown targets and shutdown to OFF or RESET

Shutdown targets are states in which no code is executed: Off, Sleep, and Reset (SWS EcuM p. 66, [SWS_EcuM_04136]). EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget merely stores the target and initiates nothing on its own [SWS_EcuM_02585]. The mode parameter applies only to SLEEP and RESET [SWS_EcuM_02979]. Available reset modalities are at least Mcu_PerformReset, WdgM_PerformReset, and toggling an I/O pin [SWS_EcuM_04005]. Additionally, a shutdown cause can be recorded [SWS_EcuM_04050].

State diagram: The lifecycle passes through the phases STARTUP, UP, SLEEP, and SHUTDOWN. From SLEEP, a wakeup event leads back to UP, whereas a reset leads to STARTUP. Sources: SWS EcuM p. 71, SWS EcuM p. 54, [SWS_EcuM_02963], [SWS_EcuM_04001]

Entry into SHUTDOWN is controlled by BswM. It is likely to occur via EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll as well, since the synchronization diagram mentions this call by BswM (SWS EcuM p. 74, [SWS_EcuM_91002]). The OffPreOS sequence calls EcuM_OnGoOffOne [SWS_EcuM_02916] and deinitializes BswM and SchM (SWS EcuM p. 90). As the last step, it calls ShutdownOS [SWS_EcuM_02952]. If a wakeup event occurs during this process, the EcuM must terminate shutdown and restart immediately [SWS_EcuM_02756]. Presumably, this occurs by switching the target to RESET.

The shutdown hook calls EcuM_Shutdown, which does not return [SWS_EcuM_02953]. The OffPostOS sequence follows: EcuM_OnGoOffTwo, then depending on the target EcuM_AL_Reset or EcuM_AL_SwitchOff [SWS_EcuM_04074] [SWS_EcuM_04075]. If the reset mode originates from a EcuM_ShutdownModeType, it must be shifted right by one byte prior to handover (SWS EcuM p. 142).

Activity diagram: Shutdown branches twice. First, OffPreOS checks for pending wakeup events; then, OffPostOS selects between RESET and OFF. Sources: SWS EcuM p. 50, SWS EcuM p. 82, [SWS_EcuM_02756], [SWS_EcuM_02953]

Sleep phase: GoSleep, Halt or Poll, WakeupRestart

EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll with target SLEEP first starts the GoSleep sequence. Thereafter, depending on EcuMSleepModeSuspend, the Halt or the Poll sequence follows (SWS EcuM p. 54). The OS remains active in this phase [SWS_EcuM_02951]. GoSleep arms the wakeup sources configured for the sleep mode [SWS_EcuM_02389] [SWS_EcuM_02546] and allocates the resource RES_AUTOSAR_ECUM per core [SWS_EcuM_03010]. If a wakeup event occurs already during GoSleep, Halt and Poll must no longer be entered [SWS_EcuM_02188].

The two sleep variants differ as follows:

  • Halt: The microcontroller is halted, no code is executed [SWS_EcuM_02960]. Beforehand, EcuM_GenerateRamHash calculates a checksum over the RAM; after waking up, EcuM_CheckRamHash verifies it. In case of multiple cores, this occurs only on the master [SWS_EcuM_02863].
  • Poll: The controller continues to execute code [SWS_EcuM_02962]. In R20-11, the EcuM calls EcuM_SleepActivity and the callout EcuM_CheckWakeup in a blocking loop until a wakeup event is present [SWS_EcuM_03020]. Starting with R21-11, this callout is named EcuM_CheckWakeupHook, and EcuM_CheckWakeup becomes an EcuM function (SWS EcuM p. 145).

Sequence diagram: The Halt sequence surrounds standstill with generation and verification of the RAM checksum. Thereafter, it reports the wakeup source to BswM, as PENDING or VALIDATED. Sources: SWS EcuM p. 85, [SWS_EcuM_02863], [SWS_EcuM_02987], [SWS_EcuM_02963]

Following a wakeup event, the EcuM regains control and executes the WakeupRestart sequence [SWS_EcuM_02963]. It encompasses:

  • restoring MCU normal mode,
  • disabling pending wakeup sources [SWS_EcuM_04084],
  • re-initializing drivers via EcuM_AL_DriverRestart and re-arming their wakeup callback [SWS_EcuM_02562],
  • releasing the scheduler (SWS EcuM p. 56).

Wakeup sources: bitmask, states, and validation protocol

The EcuM manages up to 32 wakeup sources as bits in EcuM_WakeupSourceType. Five positions are predefined (SWS EcuM p. 63, [SWS_EcuM_04040]). Further sources occupy bits 5 to 31 via EcuMWakeupSourceId [SWS_EcuM_02165] [SWS_EcuM_02166]. Each source is in one of four states: NONE, PENDING, VALIDATED, or EXPIRED [SWS_EcuM_04091]. The EcuM reports every state change as a mode request to BswM [SWS_EcuM_04003].

State diagram: A source without validation requirement transitions directly to VALIDATED. All others wait in PENDING for confirmation or time out into EXPIRED. Sources: SWS EcuM p. 60, [SWS_EcuM_04091], [SWS_EcuM_02566], [SWS_EcuM_02683]

A driver reports a detected event once with EcuM_SetWakeupEvent (SWS EcuM p. 71). This is permitted from interrupts as well [SWS_EcuM_02171]. The function sets the pending bit [SWS_EcuM_01117] and ignores sources that do not belong to the selected sleep mode [SWS_EcuM_04138]. In addition, it starts the validation timer, but not again upon repeated calls for the same source [SWS_EcuM_02709] [SWS_EcuM_02712]. If no validation is configured for a source, the event is considered validated immediately [SWS_EcuM_02566]. Reset and power sources are never validated [SWS_EcuM_02625].

Validation runs in EcuM_MainFunction [SWS_EcuM_02539] and follows this protocol:

  • EcuM_StartWakeupSources prepares the sources, EcuM_CheckValidation subsequently queries them [SWS_EcuM_02924] [SWS_EcuM_02925].
  • If validation succeeds, the validating module calls EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent. The EcuM then stops the timer, sets the validated bit, reports VALIDATED to BswM, and informs ComM [SWS_EcuM_04078] [SWS_EcuM_02710] [SWS_EcuM_04079] [SWS_EcuM_02645].
  • If the timer expires, the EcuM sets the expired bit, reports EXPIRED to BswM, and calls EcuM_StopWakeupSources [SWS_EcuM_04081] [SWS_EcuM_04082] [SWS_EcuM_02926].
  • In the RUN state, validation is effective only for communication channels [SWS_EcuM_02790].
  • EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent clears the bits in all three internal variables [SWS_EcuM_02683].
  • A running CheckWakeupTimer prevents shutdown before a source has been checked [SWS_EcuM_04096]. EcuM_SetWakeupEvent cancels it [SWS_EcuM_04098].

Sequence diagram: Validation is a loop with two outcomes: confirmation or timeout. Each outcome generates its own reports to BswM and ComM. Sources: SWS EcuM p. 63, SWS EcuM p. 64, [SWS_EcuM_02709], [SWS_EcuM_04082]

Multicore operation, wakeup timer, and boot target

On multicore ECUs, one EcuM instance runs per core. The master EcuM starts the remaining cores (SWS EcuM p. 71). For each instance:

  • The init callouts initialize only the MCAL modules of their own core [SWS_EcuM_04145].
  • OS and SchM are started on each core [SWS_EcuM_04093].
  • Each instance processes the wakeup events of its core [SWS_EcuM_04012].
  • The SLEEP target puts all cores to sleep [SWS_EcuM_04092].

The optional wakeup timer counts seconds since the battery was connected [SWS_EcuM_04069]. Each user has at most one alarm [SWS_EcuM_04070], and the master alarm follows the earliest user alarm [SWS_EcuM_04072]. A later alarm returns ECUM_E_EARLIER_ACTIVE, a past point in time ECUM_E_PAST [SWS_EcuM_04059] [SWS_EcuM_04060]. When alarms are cleared is governed by [SWS_EcuM_04010]. EcuM_SelectBootTarget stores the boot target so that the bootloader can read it [SWS_EcuM_02247].

Behavior in the event of an error

Unrecoverable errors: Here, the EcuM calls EcuM_ErrorHook [SWS_EcuM_04033], specifically with ECUM_E_CONFIGURATION_DATA_INCONSISTENT or ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_FAILED [SWS_EcuM_91003] [SWS_EcuM_02987].

Failed OS calls: According to R20-11, the state remains unchanged, and the EcuM reports the error via the ErrorHook [SWS_EcuM_04139]. The dedicated code ECUM_E_OS_CALL_FAILED and the assumption that the hook does not return are first mentioned in a later release (SWS EcuM p. 102).

Further rules:

  • The EcuM ignores errors during initialization [SWS_EcuM_02980].
  • It maps an unknown reset reason to ECUM_WKSOURCE_RESET [SWS_EcuM_02601].
  • A reset or power cycle during Halt or Poll leads back to STARTUP [SWS_EcuM_04001].
  • If the ECU cannot de-energize itself in EcuM_AL_SwitchOff, a reset is the appropriate reaction. The integrator is permitted to limit the endless loop (SWS EcuM p. 141).

Development errors to the DET:

  • general codes [SWS_EcuM_03009],
  • multiple requests [SWS_EcuM_03024] and releases without request [SWS_EcuM_03023],
  • unknown wakeup sources [SWS_EcuM_02867],
  • invalid states in EcuM_SetState [SWS_EcuM_04123].

Further detailed evidence

  • Startup: [SWS_EcuM_02411] (StartPreOS in EcuM_Init), [SWS_EcuM_02795] (consistency hash), SWS EcuM p. 46 (driver initialization).
  • Mode handling: [SWS_EcuM_04120] (EcuM_RunStatusType), [SWS_EcuM_91005] (EcuM_StateType).
  • Shutdown: [SWS_EcuM_02156] (last shutdown target), [SWS_EcuM_04007] (shutdown causes).
  • Sleep and wakeup: [SWS_EcuM_04066] (WakeupRestart), [SWS_EcuM_02947] (restart list), SWS EcuM p. 70 (SLEEP via system module).
  • Multicore: [SWS_EcuM_04015] to [SWS_EcuM_04030] (master/slave sequences).

function EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll [SWS_EcuM_91002] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll (EcuM_UserType UserID);

Instructs the ECU State Manager module to go into a sleep mode, Reset or OFF depending on the previously selected shutdown target.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 3c8762154e41 Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous function EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll ([SWS_EcuM_91002]) instructs the ECU State Manager to transition into a sleep mode (SLEEP), a reset (RESET), or into the state OFF, depending on the previously selected shutdown target. The interface is provided via header EcuM.h.

The caller passes its ID via the parameter UserID (type EcuM_UserType). The call is permitted exclusively for preconfigured users ([SWS_EcuM_91002]).

Return Values and Control Flow

The return behavior depends decisively on the configured ShutdownTargetType ([SWS_EcuM_91002]):

  • E_OK: If SLEEP was defined as the shutdown target, the call returns successfully after waking up again or leaving the sleep state. If, however, the target is RESET or OFF, the function does not return.
  • E_NOT_OK: Signals that the request for execution could not be accepted.

Concurrency and Limitations

The function has the service ID 0x2c and is specified as reentrant ([SWS_EcuM_91002]). A mandatory sequence condition for a successful execution is that a corresponding shutdown target has been set prior to the call.

This note is based on the specifications of AUTOSAR CP R20-11 for element SWS_EcuM_91002 and was generated automatically.

function EcuM_StartupTwo [SWS_EcuM_02838] 📄 PDF

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: ef3714328812 Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant function EcuM_RequestRUN ([SWS_EcuM_04124]) requests the RUN state of the ECU State Manager. It is available via header EcuM.h and may be called by any user that was made known to the EcuM at configuration time ([SWS_EcuM_04124]).

Parameters and Return Values

  • user: Unique identifier (EcuM_UserType) of the entity requesting the RUN state ([SWS_EcuM_04124]).
  • E_OK: The request was accepted by the EcuM ([SWS_EcuM_04124]).
  • E_NOT_OK: The request was rejected by the EcuM ([SWS_EcuM_04124]).

Restrictions and Error Handling

Requests via EcuM_RequestRUN cannot be nested; an individual user may hold at most one request at a time ([SWS_EcuM_04125]). If the function determines with enabled development error detection (Development Error Detection) that the same user issues an additional or duplicate request, it reports the error ECUM_E_MULTIPLE_RUN_REQUESTS to the DET ([SWS_EcuM_03024], [SWS_EcuM_04125]).

Interaction

A request previously placed by EcuM_RequestRUN must be released again via the complementary function EcuM_ReleaseRUN of the same user when no longer needed ([SWS_EcuM_04127]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification requirements for AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.

The unique user ID of the entity that releases the RUN state is passed via the input parameter user (type EcuM_UserType).

Return Values and Error Handling

The function returns a status of type Std_ReturnType ([SWS_EcuM_04127]):

Specific development errors (DET), production code errors (DEM), or detailed error causes for returning E_NOT_OK are not separately specified at the interface.

The technical prerequisite for the release is a preceding request via EcuM_RequestRUN. The interaction and integration of the runnable entities in the context of the RTE configuration are based on the specification of the internal behavior of the ECU State Manager ([SWS_EcuM_03018]).

Requests for RUN and POST RUN must be tracked independently of each other in the module ([SWS_EcuM_04128]). A successful call returns E_OK, while E_NOT_OK signals that the request was rejected by EcuM ([SWS_EcuM_04128]).

The function EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN ([SWS_EcuM_04129]) serves to release a POST-RUN phase of the ECU previously requested via EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN. The interface is declared in the header file EcuM.h and is intended in particular for the implementation of AUTOSAR ports.

  • Call context & Synchronicity: The call is synchronous and is specified as reentrant ([SWS_EcuM_04129]).
  • Parameters: user (type EcuM_UserType) is passed, which represents the unique user ID of the entity releasing the POST-RUN state.
  • Return value: The service provides a return value of type Std_ReturnType. The value E_OK indicates that the release request was accepted by the ECU State Manager; E_NOT_OK indicates that the request was rejected.

Error Handling and Concurrency

In case of an error, E_NOT_OK is returned. Specific DET or DEM notifications are not specified in element [SWS_EcuM_04129]. A rejection with E_NOT_OK is likely to occur if no active POST-RUN request is registered for the passed user ID or if the parameter is invalid.

Due to its property as a reentrant function, EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN can be called concurrently. As a functional sequence condition, the call requires that the same entity previously executed EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN successfully.

Interaction

The service forms the counterpart to the POST-RUN request and, during port realization, interacts with the internal behavior of the ECU State Manager, whose runnable entities and RTE configuration are described in [SWS_EcuM_03018].

The synchronous function EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget ([SWS_EcuM_02822]) serves to select the shutdown target in the ECU Manager. It is available via EcuM.h and belongs to the port interface of the module.

Two input parameters are passed:

  • shutdownTarget: Determines the selected shutdown target to whose value the target function is set ([SWS_EcuM_00624]).
  • shutdownMode: Specifies the identifier of a sleep mode (if the target is ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_SLEEP) or defines a reset mechanism (if the target is ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_RESET) according to the configuration ([SWS_EcuM_02822]).

Error Handling and Return Values

The function returns a Std_ReturnType as a result ([SWS_EcuM_02822]):

  • E_OK: The new shutdown target was successfully accepted.
  • E_NOT_OK: The new shutdown target could not be set.

Concurrency and Interaction

The function is specified as reentrant ([SWS_EcuM_02822]). In the internal behavior description (InternalBehavior EcuStateManager), the runnable entity SelectShutdownTarget is defined with canbeInvokedConcurrently = TRUE ([SWS_EcuM_03018]), which supports concurrent invocation via the local RTE.

With regard to execution, EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget does not trigger any immediate setup or shutdown activities, but merely saves the target value for later use in the SHUTDOWN or SLEEP phase ([SWS_EcuM_02585]).

It can thus be called concurrently from different contexts.

function EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent [SWS_EcuM_02828] 📄 PDF

void EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent (EcuM_WakeupSourceType sources);

Clears wakeup events.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 5de97c21bf1f Provenance

The synchronous function EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent (service ID 0x16) serves to reset wakeup events and is provided via the header file EcuM.h ([SWS_EcuM_02828]).

Usage: The function has no return value (return type void). As an input parameter, it accepts sources of type EcuM_WakeupSourceType, via which the events to be reset are passed in the form of a bitmask ([SWS_EcuM_02828], [SWS_EcuM_02683]).

Interaction and functional effect: According to [SWS_EcuM_02683], the call synchronously clears all events passed as a set bit in parameter sources from three internal state variables of the module:

  • from the internal variable for pending wakeup events (pending wakeup events),
  • from the internal variable for validated wakeup events (validated events), and
  • from the internal variable for expired wakeup events (expired events).

Call context and concurrency: For the call context, it is specified that EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent may be called from the interrupt context as well as from the OS context and an OS-free context ([SWS_EcuM_02807]). However, since the interface is explicitly classified as non-reentrant and non-interruptible (Non-Reentrant, Non-Interruptible) ([SWS_EcuM_02828]), concurrent or mutually interrupting calls across these contexts must be ruled out at system level.

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.

The function EcuM_AbortWakeupAlarm serves the targeted cancellation of a wakeup alarm that was previously set up by the calling user ([SWS_EcuM_04061]). The call is processed synchronously and is available via the header EcuM.h ([SWS_EcuM_04061]). In addition, the service is defined as part of the port interface of module EcuM ([SWS_EcuM_04061]).

Call and Parameters

Exactly one input parameter is passed to DEM service:

  • user (IN parameter, type EcuM_UserType): Designates the identifier of the user who wants to cancel the existing wakeup alarm ([SWS_EcuM_04061]).

Return Values and Error Handling

The return value of type Std_ReturnType provides information about the result of the cancellation ([SWS_EcuM_04061]):

  • E_OK: The service was executed successfully; the user's alarm was canceled ([SWS_EcuM_04061]).
  • ECUM_E_NOT_ACTIVE: No active or assigned alarm could be found for the passed user ([SWS_EcuM_04061]).
  • E_NOT_OK: Execution of the service failed ([SWS_EcuM_04061]).

Concurrency and Integration

The function EcuM_AbortWakeupAlarm is specified as reentrant ([SWS_EcuM_04061]). As an element of the port interface of the ECU State Manager, the service integrates into the described internal behavior of the module for the RTE configuration ([SWS_EcuM_03018]).

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous function EcuM_SelectBootTarget serves to select a boot target for the ECU [SWS_EcuM_02835]. target of type EcuM_BootTargetType is passed as a parameter. Via return value Std_ReturnType, the function reports back whether the requested boot target was accepted by the ECU State Manager (E_OK) or not (E_NOT_OK) [SWS_EcuM_02835]. The declaration is provided via EcuM.h and is part of the port interface of the ECU Manager [SWS_EcuM_02835].

Constraints and Call Context

The following requirements and boundary conditions apply to the call:

  • Caller circle: The service is intended exclusively for use by diagnostic-related software components (boot management) [SWS_EcuM_03000].
  • Bootloader dependency: The function may depend on the respective bootloader used [SWS_EcuM_03000]. The selected target must be stored by EcuM_SelectBootTarget such that the format or storage is compatible with the bootloader [SWS_EcuM_02247].
  • Concurrency: The function is reentrant [SWS_EcuM_02835]. At the RTE level, the associated runnable entity SelectBootTarget is enabled for concurrent execution (canbeInvokedConcurrently = TRUE) [SWS_EcuM_03018].

Error Handling and Interaction

Specific DET or DEM errors are not documented; an error in accepting the target is indicated by return value E_NOT_OK [SWS_EcuM_02835]. The currently set boot target can be queried via the complementary function EcuM_GetBootTarget [SWS_EcuM_02836].

function EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent [SWS_EcuM_02829] 📄 PDF

void EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent (EcuM_WakeupSourceType sources);

After wakeup, the ECU State Manager will stop the process during the WAKEUP VALIDATION state/sequence to wait for validation of the wakeup event.This API service is used to indicate to the ECU Manager module that the wakeup events indicated in the sources parameter have been validated.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 4ebe0c162f54 Provenance

Usage and Call Context

The synchronous and reentrant function EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent serves to indicate to the ECU State Manager that the wakeup events passed in parameter sources have been validated [SWS_EcuM_02829]. It has no return value and may be called from both task and interrupt contexts [SWS_EcuM_02345].

Functionality and restrictions

Upon invocation, all events set in the bitmask sources are set in the internal variable for validated wakeup events using an OR operation [SWS_EcuM_04078]. In addition, the function stops the associated timeout timer for wakeup validation [SWS_EcuM_02710].

State-related requirements apply to the execution:

  • If the module is in the RUN state, the call has no effect for any sources, unless they are communication channels [SWS_EcuM_02790].
  • If a wakeup source corresponds to a communication channel, the call takes full effect in every ECU phase [SWS_EcuM_02791].

Interaction with EcuM and ComM

After wakeup, the ECU State Manager stops execution during the WAKEUP VALIDATION state or sequence to wait for the validation of the wakeup events [SWS_EcuM_02829]. The check can be performed via callout EcuM_CheckValidation, which reports a positive check result via EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent [SWS_EcuM_02925]. If no validation protocol is configured, a call to EcuM_SetWakeupEvent already automatically implies a call to EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent [SWS_EcuM_02566].

Depending on the configuration of the wakeup source, EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent performs the following subsequent calls:

  • Call to ComM_EcuM_WakeUpIndication for each wakeup event if parameter EcuMComMChannelRef is configured [SWS_EcuM_02645].
  • Call to ComM_EcuM_PNCWakeUpIndication for each wakeup event and for each referenced PNC, provided at least one parameter EcuMComMPNCRef is present [SWS_EcuM_04140].

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification.

function EcuM_ErrorHook [SWS_EcuM_02904] 📄 PDF

void EcuM_ErrorHook (uint16 reason);

The ECU State Manager will call the error hook if the error codes "ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_ FAILED" or "ECUM_E_CONFIGURATION_DATA_INCONSISTENT" occur. In this situation it is not possible to continue processing and the ECU must be stopped. The integrator may choose the modality how the ECU is stopped, i.e. reset, halt, restart, safe state etc.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 10d188e80f3b Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The callback function EcuM_ErrorHook is a synchronous, non-reentrant hook of the ECU State Manager ([SWS_EcuM_02904]). It is provided via header file EcuM_Externals.h and has service ID 0x30 ([SWS_EcuM_02904]). reason of type uint16 is passed as the sole input parameter, indicating the cause of the error; a return value does not exist ([SWS_EcuM_02904]).

Error Handling and Shutdown

The hook is called when severe errors occur where regular further processing is impossible and the ECU must be stopped ([SWS_EcuM_02904]). This particularly applies to error codes ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_FAILED and ECUM_E_CONFIGURATION_DATA_INCONSISTENT ([SWS_EcuM_02904]). The specific modality of the shutdown—for example reset, halt, restart, or entering a safe state—is the responsibility of the integrator ([SWS_EcuM_02904]).

Interaction and Boundary Conditions

  • RAM check during wakeup: If the RAM check fails during wakeup, module EcuM calls EcuM_ErrorHook with parameter ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_FAILED ([SWS_EcuM_02987]). It is at the integrator's discretion to forward this error to the DEM, provided it is ensured that the DEM does not write to damaged NVRAM blocks ([SWS_EcuM_02987]).
  • Failed operating system calls: If a call to an OS function fails and no other error reaction is defined, the EcuM does not transition to the requested state; in such cases, error reporting likewise occurs via EcuM_ErrorHook ([SWS_EcuM_04139]).

This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification for module EcuM.

function EcuM_EndCheckWakeup [SWS_EcuM_02927] 📄 PDF

void EcuM_EndCheckWakeup (EcuM_WakeupSourceType WakeupSource);

This API is called by any SW Module whose wakeup source is checked asynchronously (e.g. asynchronous Can Trcv Driver) and the Check of the Wakeup returns a negative Result (no Wakeup by this Source). The API cancels the CheckWakeupTimer for the WakeupSource. If the correponding CheckWakeupTimer is canceled the check of this wakeup source is finished.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 644630864c90 Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The function EcuM_EndCheckWakeup ([SWS_EcuM_02927]) is called synchronously by software modules whose wakeup sources are checked asynchronously (for example, by an asynchronous CAN transceiver driver). The call occurs specifically when the check of the wakeup source yields a negative result, meaning no wakeup was detected by this source.

Via the input parameter WakeupSource of type EcuM_WakeupSourceType, the function cancels the associated CheckWakeupTimer for the wakeup source in question. With the cancellation of this timer, the check of the wakeup source is considered completed. The function has no return value (void) and is made available via header EcuM_Externals.h.

Concurrency and Limitations

  • Reentrancy: The function is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant). Parallel calls must be avoided or serialized by the overall system.
  • Call context: The service is intended exclusively for the asynchronous wakeup check path and may only be used for wakeup sources for which an asynchronous check is active and has yielded a negative result.

function EcuM_CheckRamHash [SWS_EcuM_02921] 📄 PDF

uint8 EcuM_CheckRamHash (void);

This callout is intended to provide a RAM integrity test. The goal of this test is to ensure that after a long SLEEP duration, RAM contents is still consistent. The check does not need to be exhaustive since this would consume quite some processing time during wakeups. A well designed check will execute quickly and detect RAM integrity defects with a sufficient probability. This specification does not make any assumption about the algorithm chosen for a particular ECU. The areas of RAM which will be checked have to be chosen carefully. It depends on the check algorithm itself and the task structure. Stack contents of the task executing the RAM check e.g. very likely cannot be checked. It is good practice to have the hash generation and checking in the same task and that this task is not preemptible and that there is only little activity between hash generation and hash check. The RAM check itself is provided by the system designer. In case of applied multi core and existence of Satellite-Ecu M(s): this API will be called by the Master-EcuM only.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: b68d11d8c20d Provenance

The callout function EcuM_CheckRamHash serves to verify RAM integrity after an extended sleep phase (SLEEP) to ensure that RAM contents have remained consistent after waking up [SWS_EcuM_02921]. The call is synchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) [SWS_EcuM_02921]. The function takes no parameters and signals the result via its return value of type uint8: the value 0 represents a failed integrity test, any other value means that the test was passed successfully [SWS_EcuM_02921]. The callout is declared in EcuM_Externals.h [SWS_EcuM_02921].

Sequence and Multicore Interplay

The ECU Manager calls EcuM_CheckRamHash directly after the processor returns from the halt state [SWS_EcuM_02863]. It forms the functional counterpart to [SWS_EcuM_02919] (EcuM_GenerateRamHash), which is called immediately before halting the microcontroller [SWS_EcuM_02863]. In multicore systems with satellite or slave EcuMs, this test is executed exclusively by the master EcuM [SWS_EcuM_02921], [SWS_EcuM_02863]. Only those data areas that are within the reach of the master are checked; private data of the slave EcuMs are explicitly excluded [SWS_EcuM_02863].

Implementation Notes

  • The specification does not mandate any specific hash algorithm; the implementation is provided project-specifically by the system designer [SWS_EcuM_02921].
  • The check does not need to be exhaustive in order not to prolong wakeup times unnecessarily, but should execute quickly and detect defects with sufficient probability [SWS_EcuM_02921].
  • The RAM areas to be checked must be chosen carefully: stack areas of the executing task can generally not be checked [SWS_EcuM_02921].
  • Executing hash generation and verification in the same, non-interruptible task and keeping system activity minimal in between is considered good practice [SWS_EcuM_02921].

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification data from AUTOSAR CP R20-11.

type EcuM_WakeupSourceType [SWS_EcuM_04040] 📄 PDF

EcuM_WakeupSourceType defines a bitfield with 5 pre-defined positions (see Range). The bitfield provides one bit for each wakeup source. In WAKEUP, all bits cleared indicates that no wakeup source is known. In STARTUP, all bits cleared indicates that no reason for restart or reset is known. In this case, ECUM_WKSOURCE_RESET shall be assumed.

Usage of EcuM_WakeupStatusType

According to [SWS_EcuM_04041], the data type EcuM_WakeupStatusType defines the possible states of a wakeup source in module EcuM. It is derived from base type uint8 and is made available via header EcuM.h.

The value range comprises four discrete states to map the detection and validation progress:

  • ECUM_WKSTATUS_NONE (0): No pending wakeup event was detected.
  • ECUM_WKSTATUS_PENDING (1): A wakeup event was detected, but has not yet been validated.
  • ECUM_WKSTATUS_VALIDATED (2): The wakeup event is valid.
  • ECUM_WKSTATUS_EXPIRED (3): The wakeup event was not validated and has expired.

Interpretation: The data type is likely to serve primarily in status queries or check routines of EcuM as a return value or parameter to evaluate the current validation status of individual wakeup sources programmatically. Since neither function signatures nor DET/DEM error codes or reentrancy requirements are contained in the present specification excerpt, the conditions of the respective interface using this type apply to the call context and concurrency.

type EcuM_StateType [SWS_EcuM_91005] 📄 PDF

ECU State Manager states.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: e346652e8268 Provenance

Usage and Value Range

The type EcuM_StateType is derived from uint8 and available via the header file EcuM.h [SWS_EcuM_91005]. It maps the states of the ECU State Manager, which must be fully defined by the EcuM module [SWS_EcuM_02664]. The specification defines the following states and masks [SWS_EcuM_91005]:

  • ECUM_SUBSTATE_MASK (0x0f)
  • ECUM_STATE_STARTUP (0x10)
  • ECUM_STATE_RUN (0x32)
  • ECUM_STATE_POST_RUN (0x33)
  • ECUM_STATE_SHUTDOWN (0x40)
  • ECUM_STATE_SLEEP (0x50)

Interaction and Call Context

EcuM_StateType serves as the data type for state exchange between the ECU State Manager (EcuM) and the Basic Software Mode Manager (BswM):

  • State change by BswM: The BswM notifies the EcuM synchronously and reentrantly of a state change using the function EcuM_SetState (service ID 0x2b), where the target state is passed in parameter state of type EcuM_StateType [SWS_EcuM_04122].
  • Status feedback to BswM: The EcuM reports the current state to the BswM via the interface BswM_EcuM_CurrentState(EcuM_StateType State) [SWS_EcuM_04143].

Sequence Conditions and Error Handling

A new state may only be set by the EcuM once the RTE has provided its feedback via the acknowledgement port [SWS_EcuM_04143].

As a type definition, EcuM_StateType defines no error codes of its own or DET/DEM notifications [SWS_EcuM_91005].

Usage and definition

According to [SWS_EcuM_04107], element EcuM_Mode defines a ModeDeclarationGroup within module EcuM. The group is specified with category ALPHABETIC_ORDER and defines the initial mode as STARTUP. In total, EcuM_Mode comprises the following declared states:

  • STARTUP: Specified initial mode of the ECU ([SWS_EcuM_04107]).
  • RUN: Normal operating mode ([SWS_EcuM_04107]).
  • POST_RUN: Post-run phase after regular operation ([SWS_EcuM_04107]).
  • SLEEP: Sleep state or power-saving mode ([SWS_EcuM_04107]).
  • SHUTDOWN: Shutdown phase of the ECU ([SWS_EcuM_04107]).

Interaction and Interfaces

The mode group EcuM_Mode is directly referenced in the service interface EcuM_CurrentMode ([SWS_EcuM_04108]). This interface provides the current state via the element currentMode and serves, according to the specification, to read out the current ECU mode in the system. Interpretation: Software components and system services are likely to monitor the global state of the ECU via this service interface in order to control state-dependent actions.

Error Handling and Restrictions

Since EcuM_Mode exists purely as a type and mode group declaration (ModeDeclarationGroup) ([SWS_EcuM_04107]), neither separate API functions nor error codes (DET/DEM) are defined for it. Access to the current state takes place read-only via the interface EcuM_CurrentMode ([SWS_EcuM_04108]).

This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification elements.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 8592189dd02c Provenance

use

Element currentMode is a provided port (ProvidedPort) of module EcuM with interface EcuM_CurrentMode ([SWS_EcuM_04112]). Interface EcuM_CurrentMode is declared as a service interface (IsService = true), serves to read the current ECU mode, and defines the mode group currentMode of type EcuM_Mode ([SWS_EcuM_04108]).

Mode changes are communicated to software components (SW-Cs) via RTE mode ports as soon as the mode switch occurs ([SWS_EcuM_04133]). An SW-C that needs to be informed about mode changes must request mode switch interface EcuM_CurrentMode for this purpose ([SWS_EcuM_04133]).

Call Context and Parameters

Assuming that the port name is currentMode and the direct RTE API is used, signaling of a mode switch occurs via the following function call ([SWS_EcuM_04133]):

  • Rte_StatusType Rte_Switch_currentMode_currentMode(Rte_ModeType_EcuM_Mode mode): Parameter mode passes the mode to be newly entered ([SWS_EcuM_04133]).

Return Values and Restrictions

According to the specification, the return value of type Rte_StatusType of the API call must imperatively be ignored ([SWS_EcuM_04133]). The specification makes no statements at this point regarding specific error handlings (such as DET or DEM messages) or reentrancy and concurrency conditions.

type EcuM_ShutdownModeType [SWS_EcuM_04101] 📄 PDF

This data type represents the modes of the ECU Manager module.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 23a9525c59d7 Provenance

Usage and Value Range

The data type EcuM_ShutdownModeType [SWS_EcuM_04101] is derived from uint16, represents the modes of module ECU State Manager, and is provided via header Rte_EcuM_Type.h. Its value range covers configured sleep and reset modes:

  • Sleep modes: Are determined by the configured EcuMSleepModeId [SWS_EcuM_04101].
  • Reset modes: Are formed from the base value 256 plus the configured EcuMResetModeId [SWS_EcuM_04101].

Interaction and Interfaces

EcuM_ShutdownModeType is used in synchronous and reentrant services of the EcuM:

  • EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget [SWS_EcuM_02822]: Expects shutdownMode as an input parameter to select the specific sleep mode (for target ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_SLEEP) or reset mechanism (for target ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_RESET).
  • EcuM_GetShutdownTarget [SWS_EcuM_02824]: Returns via output pointer shutdownMode which sleep or reset mode is currently selected.
  • EcuM_GetLastShutdownTarget [SWS_EcuM_02825]: Provides the mode of the previous shutdown process via output pointer shutdownMode.
  • EcuM_ShutdownTarget [SWS_EcuM_03011]: Integrates the mode parameter into the service interface for software components (SW-Cs), among others for operation GetLastShutdownTarget.

Error Handling and Boundary Conditions

Services with pointer parameters such as EcuM_GetShutdownTarget [SWS_EcuM_02824] and EcuM_GetLastShutdownTarget [SWS_EcuM_02825] fail with E_NOT_OK if, for example, a NULL pointer is passed. In EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget [SWS_EcuM_02822], E_NOT_OK signals that the new shutdown target could not be set successfully.

Services · Check…

EcuM_CheckRamHash function

This callout is intended to provide a RAM integrity test. The goal of this test is to ensure that after a long SLEEP duration, RAM contents is still consistent. The check does not need to be exhaustive since this would consume quite some processing time during wakeups. A well designed check will execute quickly and detect RAM integrity defects with a sufficient probability. This specification does not make any assumption about the algorithm chosen for a particular ECU. The areas of RAM which will be checked have to be chosen carefully. It depends on the check algorithm itself and the task structure. Stack contents of the task executing the RAM check e.g. very likely cannot be checked. It is good practice to have the hash generation and checking in the same task and that this task is not preemptible and that there is only little activity between hash generation and hash check. The RAM check itself is provided by the system designer. In case of applied multi core and existence of Satellite-Ecu M(s): this API will be called by the Master-EcuM only.

uint8 EcuM_CheckRamHash (void);

EcuM_WakeupSourceType type

EcuM_WakeupSourceType defines a bitfield with 5 pre-defined positions (see Range). The bitfield provides one bit for each wakeup source. In WAKEUP, all bits cleared indicates that no wakeup source is known. In STARTUP, all bits cleared indicates that no reason for restart or reset is known. In this case, ECUM_WKSOURCE_RESET shall be assumed.

EcuM_WakeupStatusType type

The type describes the possible states of a wakeup source.

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="232830ad61583e9e334b3d9bccd12e99524c687e97e827a5a5d992100110689f" data-trace-output="cde4942bcfb1cfa1754d2070e15ff747aff38d06ce0df70b63b212af68650e2c" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02822" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02822">[SWS_EcuM_02822]</a>) serves to select the shutdown target in the ECU Manager. It is available via <code>EcuM.h</code> and belongs to the port interface of the module.</p>
<p>Two input parameters are passed:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>shutdownTarget</code>: Determines the selected shutdown target to whose value the target function is set (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_00624" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_00624">[SWS_EcuM_00624]</a>).</li>
<li><code>shutdownMode</code>: Specifies the identifier of a sleep mode (if the target is <code>ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_SLEEP</code>) or defines a reset mechanism (if the target is <code>ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_RESET</code>) according to the configuration (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02822" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02822">[SWS_EcuM_02822]</a>).</li>
</ul>

<h4>Error Handling and Return Values</h4>
<p>The function returns a <code>Std_ReturnType</code> as a result (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02822" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02822">[SWS_EcuM_02822]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The new shutdown target was successfully accepted.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The new shutdown target could not be set.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Concurrency and Interaction</h4>
<p>The function is specified as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02822" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02822">[SWS_EcuM_02822]</a>). In the internal behavior description (<code>InternalBehavior EcuStateManager</code>), the runnable entity <code>SelectShutdownTarget</code> is defined with <code>canbeInvokedConcurrently = TRUE</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03018">[SWS_EcuM_03018]</a>), which supports concurrent invocation via the local RTE.</p>
<p>With regard to execution, <code>EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget</code> does not trigger any immediate setup or shutdown activities, but merely saves the target value for later use in the <code>SHUTDOWN</code> or <code>SLEEP</code> phase (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02585" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02585">[SWS_EcuM_02585]</a>).</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR R20-11 specification for EcuM.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="5de97c21bf1fbfd9ee0837a48c0ced0f76bfdd1f8982ae8f474de662280e93b1" data-trace-output="397cde37ed89e042882278e1a21f9ac622092dfe69742f60574b87760a02f5f7" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>The synchronous function <code>EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent</code> (service ID <code>0x16</code>) serves to reset wakeup events and is provided via the header file <code>EcuM.h</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02828" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02828">[SWS_EcuM_02828]</a>).</p>

  <p><strong>Usage:</strong> The function has no return value (return type <code>void</code>). As an input parameter, it accepts <code>sources</code> of type <code>EcuM_WakeupSourceType</code>, via which the events to be reset are passed in the form of a bitmask (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02828" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02828">[SWS_EcuM_02828]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02683" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02683">[SWS_EcuM_02683]</a>).</p>

  <p><strong>Interaction and functional effect:</strong> According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02683" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02683">[SWS_EcuM_02683]</a>, the call synchronously clears all events passed as a set bit in parameter <code>sources</code> from three internal state variables of the module:</p>
  <ul>
    <li>from the internal variable for pending wakeup events (<em>pending wakeup events</em>),</li>
    <li>from the internal variable for validated wakeup events (<em>validated events</em>), and</li>
    <li>from the internal variable for expired wakeup events (<em>expired events</em>).</li>
  </ul>

  <p><strong>Call context and concurrency:</strong> For the call context, it is specified that <code>EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent</code> may be called from the interrupt context as well as from the OS context and an OS-free context (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02807" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02807">[SWS_EcuM_02807]</a>). However, since the interface is explicitly classified as non-reentrant and non-interruptible (<em>Non-Reentrant</em>, <em>Non-Interruptible</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02828" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02828">[SWS_EcuM_02828]</a>), concurrent or mutually interrupting calls across these contexts must be ruled out at system level.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="4ebe0c162f540123327e9be4b8f7b655e84b4f683a955695dd0120f1d3de24ba" data-trace-output="b48be589869dce50d12004c50134b3fec67d49efbb70cd86e107b4cffa123d34" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Call Context</h4>
  <p>
    The synchronous and reentrant function <code>EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent</code> serves to indicate to the ECU State Manager that the wakeup events passed in parameter <code>sources</code> have been validated <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02829" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02829">[SWS_EcuM_02829]</a>. It has no return value and may be called from both task and interrupt contexts <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02345" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02345">[SWS_EcuM_02345]</a>.
  </p>

  <h4>Functionality and restrictions</h4>
  <p>
    Upon invocation, all events set in the bitmask <code>sources</code> are set in the internal variable for validated wakeup events using an OR operation <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04078" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04078">[SWS_EcuM_04078]</a>. In addition, the function stops the associated timeout timer for wakeup validation <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02710" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02710">[SWS_EcuM_02710]</a>.
  </p>
  <p>
    State-related requirements apply to the execution:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>If the module is in the <em>RUN</em> state, the call has no effect for any sources, unless they are communication channels <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02790" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02790">[SWS_EcuM_02790]</a>.</li>
    <li>If a wakeup source corresponds to a communication channel, the call takes full effect in every ECU phase <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02791" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02791">[SWS_EcuM_02791]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction with EcuM and ComM</h4>
  <p>
    After wakeup, the ECU State Manager stops execution during the <em>WAKEUP VALIDATION</em> state or sequence to wait for the validation of the wakeup events <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02829" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02829">[SWS_EcuM_02829]</a>. The check can be performed via callout <code>EcuM_CheckValidation</code>, which reports a positive check result via <code>EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02925" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02925">[SWS_EcuM_02925]</a>. If no validation protocol is configured, a call to <code>EcuM_SetWakeupEvent</code> already automatically implies a call to <code>EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02566" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02566">[SWS_EcuM_02566]</a>.
  </p>
  <p>
    Depending on the configuration of the wakeup source, <code>EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent</code> performs the following subsequent calls:
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>Call to <code>ComM_EcuM_WakeUpIndication</code> for each wakeup event if parameter <code>EcuMComMChannelRef</code> is configured <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02645" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02645">[SWS_EcuM_02645]</a>.</li>
    <li>Call to <code>ComM_EcuM_PNCWakeUpIndication</code> for each wakeup event and for each referenced PNC, provided at least one parameter <code>EcuMComMPNCRef</code> is present <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04140" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04140">[SWS_EcuM_04140]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="c8edbb65745e2fce7baa2806995ab45968a9adabb4993ce50c50673e7942d5c3" data-trace-output="ea9c0269854188cbf6620f031a801295d89356a1c9086756a5bf3b72f7d7afc3" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>EcuM_SelectBootTarget</code> serves to select a boot target for the ECU <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02835" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02835">[SWS_EcuM_02835]</a>. <code>target</code> of type <code>EcuM_BootTargetType</code> is passed as a parameter. Via return value <code>Std_ReturnType</code>, the function reports back whether the requested boot target was accepted by the ECU State Manager (<code>E_OK</code>) or not (<code>E_NOT_OK</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02835" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02835">[SWS_EcuM_02835]</a>. The declaration is provided via <code>EcuM.h</code> and is part of the port interface of the ECU Manager <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02835" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02835">[SWS_EcuM_02835]</a>.</p>

  <h4>Constraints and Call Context</h4>
  <p>The following requirements and boundary conditions apply to the call:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Caller circle:</strong> The service is intended exclusively for use by diagnostic-related software components (boot management) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03000" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03000">[SWS_EcuM_03000]</a>.</li>
    <li><strong>Bootloader dependency:</strong> The function may depend on the respective bootloader used <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03000" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03000">[SWS_EcuM_03000]</a>. The selected target must be stored by <code>EcuM_SelectBootTarget</code> such that the format or storage is compatible with the bootloader <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02247" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02247">[SWS_EcuM_02247]</a>.</li>
    <li><strong>Concurrency:</strong> The function is reentrant <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02835" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02835">[SWS_EcuM_02835]</a>. At the RTE level, the associated runnable entity <code>SelectBootTarget</code> is enabled for concurrent execution (<code>canbeInvokedConcurrently = TRUE</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03018">[SWS_EcuM_03018]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Error Handling and Interaction</h4>
  <p>Specific DET or DEM errors are not documented; an error in accepting the target is indicated by return value <code>E_NOT_OK</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02835" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02835">[SWS_EcuM_02835]</a>. The currently set boot target can be queried via the complementary function <code>EcuM_GetBootTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02836" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02836">[SWS_EcuM_02836]</a>.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was created based on the AUTOSAR specification for the ECU State Manager (Release R20-11).</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="10d188e80f3b2563f11dcfde6d5f1f0498e23a0aba58084c29cc5c1642903419" data-trace-output="2f7e58cfb3a28c4141b1e8d474ee77e63844024c2a99241c6e37f1ae9667c3d8" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
<p>The callback function <code>EcuM_ErrorHook</code> is a synchronous, non-reentrant hook of the ECU State Manager (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02904" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02904">[SWS_EcuM_02904]</a>). It is provided via header file <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code> and has service ID <code>0x30</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02904" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02904">[SWS_EcuM_02904]</a>). <code>reason</code> of type <code>uint16</code> is passed as the sole input parameter, indicating the cause of the error; a return value does not exist (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02904" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02904">[SWS_EcuM_02904]</a>).</p>

<h4>Error Handling and Shutdown</h4>
<p>The hook is called when severe errors occur where regular further processing is impossible and the ECU must be stopped (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02904" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02904">[SWS_EcuM_02904]</a>). This particularly applies to error codes <code>ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_FAILED</code> and <code>ECUM_E_CONFIGURATION_DATA_INCONSISTENT</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02904" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02904">[SWS_EcuM_02904]</a>). The specific modality of the shutdown—for example reset, halt, restart, or entering a safe state—is the responsibility of the integrator (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02904" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02904">[SWS_EcuM_02904]</a>).</p>

<h4>Interaction and Boundary Conditions</h4>
<ul>
<li><strong>RAM check during wakeup:</strong> If the RAM check fails during wakeup, module EcuM calls <code>EcuM_ErrorHook</code> with parameter <code>ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_FAILED</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02987" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02987">[SWS_EcuM_02987]</a>). It is at the integrator's discretion to forward this error to the DEM, provided it is ensured that the DEM does not write to damaged NVRAM blocks (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02987" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02987">[SWS_EcuM_02987]</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Failed operating system calls:</strong> If a call to an OS function fails and no other error reaction is defined, the EcuM does not transition to the requested state; in such cases, error reporting likewise occurs via <code>EcuM_ErrorHook</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04139" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04139">[SWS_EcuM_04139]</a>).</li>
</ul>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification for module EcuM.</p>
</div>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The function <code>EcuM_DeterminePbConfiguration</code> is a synchronous callout (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02906" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02906">[SWS_EcuM_02906]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=78&amp;page=126">AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager p. 126</a>) provided via the header file <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code>. The call occurs without passing parameters (<code>void</code>) during the startup process of the ECU (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02906" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02906">[SWS_EcuM_02906]</a>).</p>
  <p>The task of this callout is to evaluate an application-specific condition—such as the state of a port pin or a value stored in NVRAM—to determine which post-build configuration is to be used for the further startup sequence (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02906" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02906">[SWS_EcuM_02906]</a>). The function must load this configuration data into a memory area accessible to all BSW modules (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02906" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02906">[SWS_EcuM_02906]</a>).</p>
  <p>As return value, the function returns a pointer to the EcuM post-build configuration (<code>const EcuM_ConfigType*</code>). This pointer forms the common basis for all BSW modules and contains pointers to their respective post-build configurations (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02906" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02906">[SWS_EcuM_02906]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=78&amp;page=126">AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager p. 126</a>).</p>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function has the Service ID <code>0x32</code> and is specified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../spec/record.html?doc=78&amp;page=126">AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager p. 126</a>). Interpretation: The call is likely to occur exclusively sequentially and prior to the initialization of the other BSW modules, since their configuration pointers are only obtained from the return value of this callout.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="502cc2184b7805591c307831dc78cabfa671a73764dc59e1b0363c40d1a8138b" data-trace-output="6b4c62e8078c6e1106c83c85c6a1cf05145e5f8fe9450d60e139787f5b463f59" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>
    The function <code>EcuM_EnableWakeupSources</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02918" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02918">[SWS_EcuM_02918]</a>) is a callout of the ECU Manager that is called to notify and prepare wakeup sources before entering a sleep state (SLEEP).
  </p>

  <h4>Usage and Interface</h4>
  <p>
    The ECU Manager calls the interface so that the system designer can inform the wakeup sources specified in the bitfield parameter <code>wakeupSource</code> (type <code>EcuM_WakeupSourceType</code>) about the imminent transition to the SLEEP state and configure them accordingly (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02918" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02918">[SWS_EcuM_02918]</a>). The function has no return value (<code>void</code>) and is provided via the header file <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02918" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02918">[SWS_EcuM_02918]</a>).
  </p>

  <h4>Concurrency and Properties</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Synchronicity:</strong> The call is processed synchronously (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02918" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02918">[SWS_EcuM_02918]</a>).</li>
    <li><strong>Reentrancy:</strong> The function is non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02918" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02918">[SWS_EcuM_02918]</a>).</li>
    <li><strong>Service identifier:</strong> The service ID is <code>0x3F</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02918" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02918">[SWS_EcuM_02918]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction and Sequence</h4>
  <p>
    To set up the wakeup sources for the next sleep mode, the ECU Manager module executes the callout <code>EcuM_EnableWakeupSources</code> for each wakeup source configured in parameter <code>EcuMWakeupSourceMask</code> for the respective target sleep mode (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02389" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02389">[SWS_EcuM_02389]</a>).
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was automatically generated based on the specification data.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="b68d11d8c20d69971da25f6a227aac39870775e6ec88ba7253391cbfd849f884" data-trace-output="0cab7a8269491ff136d08511e65ac3b8dc0009fa6760d0b7b13181a3b59741ac" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>The callout function <code>EcuM_CheckRamHash</code> serves to verify RAM integrity after an extended sleep phase (SLEEP) to ensure that RAM contents have remained consistent after waking up <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>. The call is synchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>. The function takes no parameters and signals the result via its return value of type <code>uint8</code>: the value <code>0</code> represents a failed integrity test, any other value means that the test was passed successfully <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>. The callout is declared in <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>.</p>

  <h4>Sequence and Multicore Interplay</h4>
  <p>The ECU Manager calls <code>EcuM_CheckRamHash</code> directly after the processor returns from the halt state <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02863" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02863">[SWS_EcuM_02863]</a>. It forms the functional counterpart to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02919" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02919">[SWS_EcuM_02919]</a> (<code>EcuM_GenerateRamHash</code>), which is called immediately before halting the microcontroller <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02863" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02863">[SWS_EcuM_02863]</a>. In multicore systems with satellite or slave EcuMs, this test is executed exclusively by the master EcuM <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02863" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02863">[SWS_EcuM_02863]</a>. Only those data areas that are within the reach of the master are checked; private data of the slave EcuMs are explicitly excluded <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02863" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02863">[SWS_EcuM_02863]</a>.</p>

  <h4>Implementation Notes</h4>
  <ul>
    <li>The specification does not mandate any specific hash algorithm; the implementation is provided project-specifically by the system designer <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>.</li>
    <li>The check does not need to be exhaustive in order not to prolong wakeup times unnecessarily, but should execute quickly and detect defects with sufficient probability <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>.</li>
    <li>The RAM areas to be checked must be chosen carefully: stack areas of the executing task can generally not be checked <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>.</li>
    <li>Executing hash generation and verification in the same, non-interruptible task and keeping system activity minimal in between is considered good practice <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02921" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02921">[SWS_EcuM_02921]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification data from AUTOSAR CP R20-11.</p>

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The callout function <code>EcuM_CheckValidation</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02925" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02925">[SWS_EcuM_02925]</a>) is called by module <code>EcuM</code> to validate a wakeup source that has occurred. It is specified as a synchronous interface with the Service ID <code>0x47</code> and declared via header <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code>. Via the input parameter <code>wakeupSource</code> (type <code>EcuM_WakeupSourceType</code>), the wakeup source to be checked is communicated to the callout. The function has neither input/output parameters nor output parameters and provides no return value (<code>void</code>).</p>

<h4>Interaction</h4>
<p>If the check determines that a valid wakeup event is present, this must be reported to the <code>EcuM</code> via the call to <code>EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent()</code> according to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02925" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02925">[SWS_EcuM_02925]</a>. The confirmation of the wakeup event therefore does not occur as a direct return value of the callout, but via this separate notification function.</p>

<h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
<p>With regard to concurrency, <code>EcuM_CheckValidation</code> is defined as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02925" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02925">[SWS_EcuM_02925]</a>). The calling system or the <code>EcuM</code> must ensure that no simultaneous or overlapping executions of the function take place.</p>

<h4>Error handling</h4>
<p>Neither error codes nor reports to DET or DEM are specified for <code>EcuM_CheckValidation</code> in the specification.</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>EcuM_EndCheckWakeup</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02927" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02927">[SWS_EcuM_02927]</a>) is called synchronously by software modules whose wakeup sources are checked asynchronously (for example, by an asynchronous CAN transceiver driver). The call occurs specifically when the check of the wakeup source yields a negative result, meaning no wakeup was detected by this source.
  </p>
  <p>
    Via the input parameter <code>WakeupSource</code> of type <code>EcuM_WakeupSourceType</code>, the function cancels the associated <code>CheckWakeupTimer</code> for the wakeup source in question. With the cancellation of this timer, the check of the wakeup source is considered completed. The function has no return value (<code>void</code>) and is made available via header <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code>.
  </p>
  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Reentrancy:</strong> The function is specified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>). Parallel calls must be avoided or serialized by the overall system.</li>
    <li><strong>Call context:</strong> The service is intended exclusively for the asynchronous wakeup check path and may only be used for wakeup sources for which an asynchronous check is active and has yielded a negative result.</li>
  </ul>
  <p class="ai-note">
    This usage note is based exclusively on the specification data from Release R20-11 for SWS_EcuM_02927.
  </p>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The callout <code>EcuM_CheckWakeup</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02929" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02929">[SWS_EcuM_02929]</a>) with service ID <code>0x42</code> is declared via the header file <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code>. The function is executed synchronously and has no return value (<code>void</code>). As the only input parameter, <code>wakeupSource</code> of type <code>EcuM_WakeupSourceType</code> is passed; input/output or purely output parameters are not defined.</p>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02929" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02929">[SWS_EcuM_02929]</a>, the callout is intended for two call contexts:</p>
  <ul>
    <li>Call by the EcuM module for cyclic polling of a wakeup source.</li>
    <li>Call by the interrupt service routine (ISR) of a wakeup source to configure the PLL ("set up the PLL") and check additional wakeup sources that may be connected to the same interrupt.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is specified as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02929" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02929">[SWS_EcuM_02929]</a>). During integration, it must therefore be ensured that no parallel or overlapping calls occur, especially since calls can take place both from the regular EcuM task context and from ISRs.</p>

  <h4>Interaction</h4>
  <p>In the poll sequence, the EcuM calls the callouts <code>EcuM_SleepActivity</code> and <code>EcuM_CheckWakeup()</code> in a blocking loop until a pending or validated wakeup event is reported (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03020">[SWS_EcuM_03020]</a>).</p>

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>
    The synchronous function <code>EcuM_SelectShutdownCause</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04050" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04050">[SWS_EcuM_04050]</a>) serves to select the cause for an upcoming shutdown of the ECU. It is part of the port interface of the ECU Manager module and available via the header file <code>EcuM.h</code> with service ID <code>0x1b</code>. As a passing parameter, the function expects the value <code>target</code> of type <code>EcuM_ShutdownCauseType</code>, which passes the desired shutdown cause.
  </p>

  <h4>Error handling</h4>
  <p>
    The call returns a return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04050" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04050">[SWS_EcuM_04050]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The new shutdown cause was set successfully.</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The new shutdown cause could not be adopted.</li>
  </ul>
  <p>
    Specific error codes for DET or DEM are not separately listed for this element in the specification.
  </p>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    <code>EcuM_SelectShutdownCause</code> is specified as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04050" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04050">[SWS_EcuM_04050]</a>). This is consistent with the definition of the internal behavior (<code>InternalBehavior EcuStateManager</code>), in which the associated runnable entity <code>SelectShutdownCause</code> is configured with property <code>canbeInvokedConcurrently = TRUE</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03018">[SWS_EcuM_03018]</a>). It can thus be called concurrently from different contexts.
  </p>

  <h4>Interaction</h4>
  <p>

The runnable entity <code>GetShutdownCause</code> declared there (symbol <code>EcuM_GetShutdownCause</code>) likely serves as a complementary function to query the cause previously set with <code>EcuM_SelectShutdownCause</code> again. <div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="33dd6b91e0648fdf704d1e02c8a6647c3757032c47dd84b89640491456fbd379" data-trace-output="aac142d19b2dc0807afff232b240020e253368d2502a0d23d398f705922ba42a" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>The function <code>EcuM_AbortWakeupAlarm</code> serves the targeted cancellation of a wakeup alarm that was previously set up by the calling user (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>). The call is processed synchronously and is available via the header <code>EcuM.h</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>). In addition, the service is defined as part of the port interface of module <code>EcuM</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Call and Parameters</h4>
  <p>Exactly one input parameter is passed to DEM service:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>user</code> (IN parameter, type <code>EcuM_UserType</code>): Designates the identifier of the user who wants to cancel the existing wakeup alarm (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>The return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> provides information about the result of the cancellation (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The service was executed successfully; the user's alarm was canceled (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_E_NOT_ACTIVE</code>: No active or assigned alarm could be found for the passed user (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: Execution of the service failed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Integration</h4>
  <p>The function <code>EcuM_AbortWakeupAlarm</code> is specified as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>). As an element of the port interface of the ECU State Manager, the service integrates into the described internal behavior of the module for the RTE configuration (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03018">[SWS_EcuM_03018]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note is based on the definitions in the specification AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.</p>
</div>
