<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="4530a9818d487e76e4181a0fabc7845bef47279b4908e66acceb6d1935fa0531" data-trace-output="5cb5a117fb1ea5a5a27bd5d2e0c0509d0ed4d6cba25866573235ac50f97a31fd" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>use</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>EcuM_SetClock</code> sets the time of the ECU Manager to the passed value (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>). It primarily serves to test alarm services, as it allows alarms to be tested whose expiration would regularly take several days (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>). The function is part of the port interface of the ECU Manager module and available via header <code>EcuM.h</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>).</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>user</code>: Identifier of the user or caller wanting to set the time (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>time</code>: Absolute time specification in seconds since connecting the vehicle battery (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>).</li>
    <li><strong>Return value:</strong> Returns <code>E_OK</code> upon successful execution of the service and <code>E_NOT_OK</code> if execution has failed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is designed to be reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>). Specific error codes as well as notifications to DET or DEM are not specified in the payload for this service; error handling is limited to the return value <code>E_NOT_OK</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Interaction</h4>
  <p>Since <code>EcuM_SetClock</code> belongs to the port interface of the ECU Manager (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>), the call in an RTE environment is likely provided for SWCs via corresponding port interfaces analogously to the defined service runnables of the internal module behavior (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03018">[SWS_EcuM_03018]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification data.</p>

  <p>The callout function <code>EcuM_AL_Reset</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04065" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04065">[SWS_EcuM_04065]</a>) accommodates user- or platform-specific code for resetting the ECU. The declaration is provided via the header <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code> with the service ID <code>0x4C</code>.</p>

  <h4>Usage and Call Context</h4>
  <p>The call to <code>EcuM_AL_Reset</code> is executed synchronously:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong><code>reset</code> (IN):</strong> Parameter of type <code>EcuM_ResetType</code> specifying the type of reset to be performed.</li>
    <li><strong>Return value:</strong> None (<code>void</code>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>The function is defined as non-reentrant (<code>Non Reentrant</code>). It must therefore not be called again concurrently or preemptively at any time.</p>

  <h4>Interaction in the System</h4>
  <p>The ECU Manager module calls callout <code>EcuM_AL_Reset</code> as soon as the shutdown target (<em>shutdown target</em>) is set to <code>RESET</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04074" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04074">[SWS_EcuM_04074]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Error handling</h4>
  <p>No error codes, return values for error indication, or notifications to DET or DEM are specified in the function definition for this callout.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="ac83dad09f41b4d60ef70167086620530d0695340562e32d9d5f56d5643b41db" data-trace-output="fd28f97fcbe00235603a4a809d195422512aa3425256389d6e77bacc282e0a46" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The function <code>EcuM_StartCheckWakeup</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04096" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04096">[SWS_EcuM_04096]</a>) is called by the ECU firmware to start the validation timer (<code>CheckWakeupTimer</code>) for a passed wakeup source (<code>WakeupSource</code> of type <code>EcuM_WakeupSourceType</code>). The interface is provided via the header <code>EcuM_Externals.h</code> and carries the service ID <code>0x00</code>. Execution is synchronous; the function has no return value (<code>void</code>).
  </p>

  <h4>Behavior and Configuration</h4>
  <p>
    The behavior upon call depends on the configured timeout value <code>EcuMCheckWakeupTimeout</code> of the respective wakeup source (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04096" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04096">[SWS_EcuM_04096]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>If <code>EcuMCheckWakeupTimeout &gt; 0</code>, the EcuM starts the associated <code>CheckWakeupTimer</code> for the specified wakeup source.</li>
    <li>If <code>EcuMCheckWakeupTimeout &lt;= 0</code>, the function call is ignored by the EcuM.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>
    The interface is specified as non-reentrant (<em>Non Reentrant</em>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04096" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04096">[SWS_EcuM_04096]</a>). Callers from the firmware must therefore ensure that the function is not executed concurrently or preemptively. Specific error codes or notifications to DET or DEM are not provided in the specification for this function call.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">
    This usage note was created automatically based on the specification of <code>EcuM_StartCheckWakeup</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04096" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04096">[SWS_EcuM_04096]</a>).
  </p>
</div>

  <h4>Usage and Value Range</h4>
  <p>The data type <code>EcuM_ShutdownModeType</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04101" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04101">[SWS_EcuM_04101]</a> is derived from <code>uint16</code>, represents the modes of module ECU State Manager, and is provided via header <code>Rte_EcuM_Type.h</code>. Its value range covers configured sleep and reset modes:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Sleep modes:</strong> Are determined by the configured <code>EcuMSleepModeId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04101" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04101">[SWS_EcuM_04101]</a>.</li>
    <li><strong>Reset modes:</strong> Are formed from the base value 256 plus the configured <code>EcuMResetModeId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04101" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04101">[SWS_EcuM_04101]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction and Interfaces</h4>
  <p><code>EcuM_ShutdownModeType</code> is used in synchronous and reentrant services of the EcuM:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02822" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02822">[SWS_EcuM_02822]</a>: Expects <code>shutdownMode</code> as an input parameter to select the specific sleep mode (for target <code>ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_SLEEP</code>) or reset mechanism (for target <code>ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_RESET</code>).</li>
    <li><code>EcuM_GetShutdownTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02824" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02824">[SWS_EcuM_02824]</a>: Returns via output pointer <code>shutdownMode</code> which sleep or reset mode is currently selected.</li>
    <li><code>EcuM_GetLastShutdownTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02825" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02825">[SWS_EcuM_02825]</a>: Provides the mode of the previous shutdown process via output pointer <code>shutdownMode</code>.</li>
    <li><code>EcuM_ShutdownTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03011" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03011">[SWS_EcuM_03011]</a>: Integrates the mode parameter into the service interface for software components (SW-Cs), among others for operation <code>GetLastShutdownTarget</code>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Error Handling and Boundary Conditions</h4>
  <p>Services with pointer parameters such as <code>EcuM_GetShutdownTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02824" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02824">[SWS_EcuM_02824]</a> and <code>EcuM_GetLastShutdownTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02825" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02825">[SWS_EcuM_02825]</a> fail with <code>E_NOT_OK</code> if, for example, a NULL pointer is passed. In <code>EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02822" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02822">[SWS_EcuM_02822]</a>, <code>E_NOT_OK</code> signals that the new shutdown target could not be set successfully.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was created automatically based on the AUTOSAR CP R20-11 specification.</p>

  <h4>Usage and definition</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>, element <code>EcuM_Mode</code> defines a <code>ModeDeclarationGroup</code> within module <code>EcuM</code>. The group is specified with category <code>ALPHABETIC_ORDER</code> and defines the initial mode as <code>STARTUP</code>. In total, <code>EcuM_Mode</code> comprises the following declared states:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>STARTUP</code>: Specified initial mode of the ECU (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>RUN</code>: Normal operating mode (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>POST_RUN</code>: Post-run phase after regular operation (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>SLEEP</code>: Sleep state or power-saving mode (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>SHUTDOWN</code>: Shutdown phase of the ECU (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction and Interfaces</h4>
  <p>The mode group <code>EcuM_Mode</code> is directly referenced in the service interface <code>EcuM_CurrentMode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04108" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04108">[SWS_EcuM_04108]</a>). This interface provides the current state via the element <code>currentMode</code> and serves, according to the specification, to read out the current ECU mode in the system. Interpretation: Software components and system services are likely to monitor the global state of the ECU via this service interface in order to control state-dependent actions.</p>

  <h4>Error Handling and Restrictions</h4>
  <p>Since <code>EcuM_Mode</code> exists purely as a type and mode group declaration (<code>ModeDeclarationGroup</code>) (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>), neither separate API functions nor error codes (DET/DEM) are defined for it. Access to the current state takes place read-only via the interface <code>EcuM_CurrentMode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04108" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04108">[SWS_EcuM_04108]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification elements.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="8592189dd02c65c962f2dd3c58a24f1f59a9ccf5e92ae4f8dfddb9f34657daab" data-trace-output="7cf99863b50aec5ac78f12e40ae0ea0c3120f566a0349d8fd159e864b0f8eee0" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>Element <code>currentMode</code> is a provided port (<code>ProvidedPort</code>) of module <code>EcuM</code> with interface <code>EcuM_CurrentMode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04112" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04112">[SWS_EcuM_04112]</a>). Interface <code>EcuM_CurrentMode</code> is declared as a service interface (<code>IsService = true</code>), serves to read the current ECU mode, and defines the mode group <code>currentMode</code> of type <code>EcuM_Mode</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04108" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04108">[SWS_EcuM_04108]</a>).</p>
<p>Mode changes are communicated to software components (SW-Cs) via RTE mode ports as soon as the mode switch occurs (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04133">[SWS_EcuM_04133]</a>). An SW-C that needs to be informed about mode changes must request mode switch interface <code>EcuM_CurrentMode</code> for this purpose (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04133">[SWS_EcuM_04133]</a>).</p>

<h4>Call Context and Parameters</h4>
<p>Assuming that the port name is <code>currentMode</code> and the direct RTE API is used, signaling of a mode switch occurs via the following function call (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04133">[SWS_EcuM_04133]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>Rte_StatusType Rte_Switch_currentMode_currentMode(Rte_ModeType_EcuM_Mode mode)</code>: Parameter <code>mode</code> passes the mode to be newly entered (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04133">[SWS_EcuM_04133]</a>).</li>
</ul>

<h4>Return Values and Restrictions</h4>
<p>According to the specification, the return value of type <code>Rte_StatusType</code> of the API call must imperatively be ignored (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04133">[SWS_EcuM_04133]</a>). The specification makes no statements at this point regarding specific error handlings (such as DET or DEM messages) or reentrancy and concurrency conditions.</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="87f2a41e864552a2b3aa4b42add7ddcf30c822c19ccbe93932e21e704efaa380" data-trace-output="d625d3562321657990d1ac1a77eb88d2975e2cccb5886539ce1028e8acd3c7c2" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>The type <code>EcuM_RunStatusType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04120" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04120">[SWS_EcuM_04120]</a>) represents the result of the so-called RUN Request Protocol, which the ECU Manager transmits to the BswM. The base type is derived from <code>uint8</code> and provided via the header <code>EcuM.h</code>.</p>

  <h4>Value Range and Semantics</h4>
  <p>According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04120" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04120">[SWS_EcuM_04120]</a>, the value range comprises the following states:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>ECUM_RUNSTATUS_UNKNOWN</code> (<code>0</code>): Unknown status, also serves as the initialization value (Init Value).</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_RUNSTATUS_REQUESTED</code> (<code>1</code>): Status was requested by the EcuM.</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_RUNSTATUS_RELEASED</code> (<code>2</code>): Status was released by the EcuM.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction in the Overall System</h4>
  <p>In the interaction of the BSW modules, this type serves as an interface for status notification: According to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04121" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04121">[SWS_EcuM_04121]</a>, the ECU Manager module must inform the BswM about the current state of the RUN Request Protocol based on the values defined in <code>EcuM_RunStatusType</code>.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="ef37143288122041d180c994ed536c090ac9ad40dfdf23db93ba6a02d170691b" data-trace-output="faafd6657bce8453dccbc3dc83bead79e1cfd92eb34c3e302895b9795cafdda6" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <p>The synchronous and reentrant function <code>EcuM_RequestRUN</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>) requests the RUN state of the ECU State Manager. It is available via header <code>EcuM.h</code> and may be called by any user that was made known to the EcuM at configuration time (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Parameters and Return Values</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><code>user</code>: Unique identifier (<code>EcuM_UserType</code>) of the entity requesting the RUN state (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_OK</code>: The request was accepted by the EcuM (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>).</li>
    <li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The request was rejected by the EcuM (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>).</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Restrictions and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>Requests via <code>EcuM_RequestRUN</code> cannot be nested; an individual user may hold at most one request at a time (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04125" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04125">[SWS_EcuM_04125]</a>). If the function determines with enabled development error detection (Development Error Detection) that the same user issues an additional or duplicate request, it reports the error <code>ECUM_E_MULTIPLE_RUN_REQUESTS</code> to the DET (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03024" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03024">[SWS_EcuM_03024]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04125" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04125">[SWS_EcuM_04125]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Interaction</h4>
  <p>A request previously placed by <code>EcuM_RequestRUN</code> must be released again via the complementary function <code>EcuM_ReleaseRUN</code> of the same user when no longer needed (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04127" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04127">[SWS_EcuM_04127]</a>).</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification requirements for AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="a98b3c9fd937bbaa26463118447542abb91d339791028b7f56f65a59cd2ed40c" data-trace-output="29326c3872a1ff6c180e0844e04a54680bd184bf204d75c35332cbd6eab8fd07" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The synchronous function <code>EcuM_ReleaseRUN</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04127" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04127">[SWS_EcuM_04127]</a>) serves to release a RUN state request previously registered via <code>EcuM_RequestRUN</code>. The service is designed for the implementation of AUTOSAR ports and is declared via <code>EcuM.h</code>. The unique user ID of the entity that releases the RUN state is passed via the input parameter <code>user</code> (type <code>EcuM_UserType</code>).</p>

<h4>Return Values and Error Handling</h4>
<p>The function returns a status of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04127" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04127">[SWS_EcuM_04127]</a>):</p>
<ul>
<li><code>E_OK</code>: The release request was accepted by the EcuM.</li>
<li><code>E_NOT_OK</code>: The release request was rejected or not accepted.</li>
</ul>
<p>Specific development errors (DET), production code errors (DEM), or detailed error causes for returning <code>E_NOT_OK</code> are not separately specified at the interface.</p>

<h4>Concurrency and Interaction</h4>
<p>According to the specification, <code>EcuM_ReleaseRUN</code> is defined as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04127" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04127">[SWS_EcuM_04127]</a>) and permits concurrent invocation by different entities. The technical prerequisite for the release is a preceding request via <code>EcuM_RequestRUN</code>. The interaction and integration of the runnable entities in the context of the RTE configuration are based on the specification of the internal behavior of the ECU State Manager (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03018">[SWS_EcuM_03018]</a>).</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification data of AUTOSAR Classic R20-11.</p>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="4e824713aec18c6ddd2394baec9c68640e68a09e82f8d240238fc842c31941cd" data-trace-output="63ac9ba85284ad0120ce6aef9c7d0a01a01419dcf585d5c3f117684e34dd0768" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>The synchronous function <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a>) requests the state <em>POST RUN</em> in the ECU State Manager. Any user (<code>user</code> of type <code>EcuM_UserType</code>) that was made known to the state manager at configuration time (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a>) is authorized to call it. The service primarily serves to implement AUTOSAR ports (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a>).</p>
  <p>Requests for <em>RUN</em> and <em>POST RUN</em> must be tracked independently of each other in the module (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a>). A successful call returns <code>E_OK</code>, while <code>E_NOT_OK</code> signals that the request was rejected by EcuM (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Error handling</h4>
  <p>If development error detection is enabled and multiple requests by the same user are detected via <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN</code>, the function reports error <code>ECUM_E_MULTIPLE_RUN_REQUESTS</code> to the DET (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03025" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03025">[SWS_EcuM_03025]</a>).</p>

  <h4>Concurrency and Interaction</h4>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Reentrancy:</strong> The function is specified as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a>).</li>
    <li><strong>Release:</strong> A request set via <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN</code> is released again via the complementary synchronous service <code>EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04129" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04129">[SWS_EcuM_04129]</a>) by specifying the same user ID.</li>
  </ul>
  <p class="ai-note">This text was generated automatically. All statements are based exclusively on the specifications of version R20-11.</p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="54268a2b2cf97fde5a67c1d3d280157c0d850da4ac842c27f637b05131bee3f7" data-trace-output="21e4dd11e267226356f43a5f379557e9f2fb291b8ccb5d716942c083add27d60" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

<h4>use</h4>
<p>The function <code>EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04129" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04129">[SWS_EcuM_04129]</a>) serves to release a POST-RUN phase of the ECU previously requested via <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN</code>. The interface is declared in the header file <code>EcuM.h</code> and is intended in particular for the implementation of AUTOSAR ports.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Call context &amp; Synchronicity:</strong> The call is synchronous and is specified as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04129" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04129">[SWS_EcuM_04129]</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Parameters:</strong> <code>user</code> (type <code>EcuM_UserType</code>) is passed, which represents the unique user ID of the entity releasing the POST-RUN state.</li>
<li><strong>Return value:</strong> The service provides a return value of type <code>Std_ReturnType</code>. The value <code>E_OK</code> indicates that the release request was accepted by the ECU State Manager; <code>E_NOT_OK</code> indicates that the request was rejected.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Error Handling and Concurrency</h4>
<p>In case of an error, <code>E_NOT_OK</code> is returned. Specific DET or DEM notifications are not specified in element <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04129" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04129">[SWS_EcuM_04129]</a>. A rejection with <code>E_NOT_OK</code> is likely to occur if no active POST-RUN request is registered for the passed user ID or if the parameter is invalid.</p>
<p>Due to its property as a reentrant function, <code>EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN</code> can be called concurrently. As a functional sequence condition, the call requires that the same entity previously executed <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN</code> successfully.</p>

<h4>Interaction</h4>
<p>The service forms the counterpart to the POST-RUN request and, during port realization, interacts with the internal behavior of the ECU State Manager, whose runnable entities and RTE configuration are described in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03018" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03018">[SWS_EcuM_03018]</a>.</p>

<p class="ai-note">This usage note was generated automatically based on the specification requirements of AUTOSAR R20-11.</p>

</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="3c8762154e410a8c6154aee5f62d7950a22d1960c20eb4d99f6a7e1b70807be9" data-trace-output="eba5f20e6c2ebfa2ea15b6693e095091e58318bdb7f04bad76bddbcd38e9e93f" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Semantics</h4>
  <p>
    The synchronous function <code>EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91002">[SWS_EcuM_91002]</a>) instructs the ECU State Manager to transition into a sleep mode (<code>SLEEP</code>), a reset (<code>RESET</code>), or into the state <code>OFF</code>, depending on the previously selected shutdown target. The interface is provided via header <code>EcuM.h</code>.
  </p>
  <p>
    The caller passes its ID via the parameter <code>UserID</code> (type <code>EcuM_UserType</code>). The call is permitted exclusively for preconfigured users (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91002">[SWS_EcuM_91002]</a>).
  </p>

  <h4>Return Values and Control Flow</h4>
  <p>
    The return behavior depends decisively on the configured <code>ShutdownTargetType</code> (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91002">[SWS_EcuM_91002]</a>):
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li>
      <code>E_OK</code>: If <code>SLEEP</code> was defined as the shutdown target, the call returns successfully after waking up again or leaving the sleep state. If, however, the target is <code>RESET</code> or <code>OFF</code>, the function does not return.
    </li>
    <li>
      <code>E_NOT_OK</code>: Signals that the request for execution could not be accepted.
    </li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Concurrency and Limitations</h4>
  <p>
    The function has the service ID <code>0x2c</code> and is specified as reentrant (<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91002">[SWS_EcuM_91002]</a>). A mandatory sequence condition for a successful execution is that a corresponding shutdown target has been set prior to the call.
  </p>

  <p class="ai-note">
    This note is based on the specifications of AUTOSAR CP R20-11 for element SWS_EcuM_91002 and was generated automatically.
  </p>
</div>

<div class="ai usage" data-trace-prompt="e346652e826873146b0ed75ab5eb73f5587361c0dafa58f4e58434eb6667e4f3" data-trace-output="8110571106bed0fbc4c28e01583405070c86baba3781f079784797907a8ff2fb" data-trace-model="gemini-3.8-flash-medium" data-trace-review="unreviewed" data-trace-effort="medium">

  <h4>Usage and Value Range</h4>
  <p>The type <code>EcuM_StateType</code> is derived from <code>uint8</code> and available via the header file <code>EcuM.h</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a>. It maps the states of the ECU State Manager, which must be fully defined by the EcuM module <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02664" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02664">[SWS_EcuM_02664]</a>. The specification defines the following states and masks <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>ECUM_SUBSTATE_MASK</code> (0x0f)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_STARTUP</code> (0x10)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_RUN</code> (0x32)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_POST_RUN</code> (0x33)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_SHUTDOWN</code> (0x40)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_SLEEP</code> (0x50)</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Interaction and Call Context</h4>
  <p><code>EcuM_StateType</code> serves as the data type for state exchange between the ECU State Manager (EcuM) and the Basic Software Mode Manager (BswM):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>State change by BswM:</strong> The BswM notifies the EcuM synchronously and reentrantly of a state change using the function <code>EcuM_SetState</code> (service ID <code>0x2b</code>), where the target state is passed in parameter <code>state</code> of type <code>EcuM_StateType</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04122">[SWS_EcuM_04122]</a>.</li>
    <li><strong>Status feedback to BswM:</strong> The EcuM reports the current state to the BswM via the interface <code>BswM_EcuM_CurrentState(EcuM_StateType State)</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04143">[SWS_EcuM_04143]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Sequence Conditions and Error Handling</h4>
  <p>A new state may only be set by the EcuM once the RTE has provided its feedback via the acknowledgement port <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04143">[SWS_EcuM_04143]</a>.</p>
  <p>As a type definition, <code>EcuM_StateType</code> defines no error codes of its own or DET/DEM notifications <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a>.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">This usage note was created automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification for R20-11.</p>
</div>

  <div class="ai-provenance-status">

<h4>Role of the EcuM: phase manager between reset, BswM, and hardware</h4>
<p>The ECU State Manager (EcuM) handles startup and shutdown of OS, SchM, and BswM, manages shutdown targets, and monitors wakeup sources including their validation. In the flexible variant, it has no state machine of its own. BswM decides on transitions; EcuM executes the associated sequences and reports back the results (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_10_EcuM_Mode_Handling.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_10_EcuM_Mode_Handling">SWS EcuM p. 103</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04116" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04116">[SWS_EcuM_04116]</a>).</p>
<p>The EcuM offloads hardware-dependent steps to callouts. These are function stubs in the integration code that the system designer fills (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_GLOSSARY_SECTION_4_53_Callout.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_GLOSSARY_SECTION_4_53_Callout">Glossary p. 42</a>). Examples are <code>EcuM_AL_DriverInitZero</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02905" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02905">[SWS_EcuM_02905]</a> and <code>EcuM_AL_SwitchOff</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02920" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02920">[SWS_EcuM_02920]</a>. The required external interfaces are listed in <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02858" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02858">[SWS_EcuM_02858]</a> and <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02859" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02859">[SWS_EcuM_02859]</a>. An overview is provided in the module relationships diagram (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-71c44c809a87837c.html" data-snip="FIG-71c44c809a87837c">SWS EcuM p. 33</a>).</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Context diagram: The EcuM controls OS, SchM, BswM, and Mcu, delegates hardware-related tasks to callouts, and receives wakeup notifications from drivers as well as state requests from SW-Cs. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-71c44c809a87837c.html" data-snip="FIG-71c44c809a87837c">SWS EcuM p. 33</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02858" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02858">[SWS_EcuM_02858]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04122">[SWS_EcuM_04122]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02826" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02826">[SWS_EcuM_02826]</a></p>

<h4>Startup: from EcuM_Init via StartOS to EcuM_StartupTwo</h4>
<p>Prior to <code>EcuM_Init</code>, stack and C variable initialization must be ready (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_3_1_Activities_before_EcuM_Init.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_3_1_Activities_before_EcuM_Init">SWS EcuM p. 39</a>). <code>EcuM_Init</code> never returns, because it ends with <code>StartOS</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02811" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02811">[SWS_EcuM_02811]</a>. In between, it executes the StartPreOS sequence <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02684" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02684">[SWS_EcuM_02684]</a>, which initializes all modules necessary for the OS start <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02603" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02603">[SWS_EcuM_02603]</a>.</p>
<p>The StartPreOS sequence proceeds in the following steps:</p>
<ul>
<li>Init Block 0 contains only modules that are configured at pre-compile or link time <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02905" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02905">[SWS_EcuM_02905]</a>.</li>
<li><code>EcuM_DeterminePbConfiguration</code> selects the post-build configuration and returns a pointer to <code>EcuM_ConfigType</code>. This structure references the configurations of all further modules <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02906" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02906">[SWS_EcuM_02906]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02801" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02801">[SWS_EcuM_02801]</a>.</li>
<li>Prior to the first BSW initialization, the EcuM checks the consistency of all post-build data via hash <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02796" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02796">[SWS_EcuM_02796]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02798" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02798">[SWS_EcuM_02798]</a>.</li>
<li>Init Block 1 follows <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02907" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02907">[SWS_EcuM_02907]</a>. Order and parameters of the initialization originate from the configuration <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02559" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02559">[SWS_EcuM_02559]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02730" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02730">[SWS_EcuM_02730]</a>.</li>
<li>The EcuM translates the reset reason into a wakeup source and remembers it <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02623" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02623">[SWS_EcuM_02623]</a>.</li>
<li>Optionally, <code>EcuM_LoopDetection</code> runs <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04137" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04137">[SWS_EcuM_04137]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p><code>EcuM_StartupTwo</code> must be called from a task that starts as a consequence of <code>StartOS</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02806" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02806">[SWS_EcuM_02806]</a>. The function executes the StartPostOS sequence: start SchM, initialize BswM, initialize SchM, and start the scheduler timing <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02932" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02932">[SWS_EcuM_02932]</a> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_3_3_Activities_in_the_StartPostOS_Sequence.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_3_3_Activities_in_the_StartPostOS_Sequence">SWS EcuM p. 42</a>). The remaining BSW modules are subsequently initialized by BswM via generated functions <code>EcuM_AL_DriverInitBswM_&lt;x&gt;</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04114" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04114">[SWS_EcuM_04114]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04142" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04142">[SWS_EcuM_04142]</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequence diagram: The STARTUP phase is divided into two parts. Prior to the OS, Init Blocks 0/1 and the consistency check run; after the OS, SchM and BswM start. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-befcb6df634dc9e0.html" data-snip="FIG-befcb6df634dc9e0">SWS EcuM p. 38</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-cfa12bb3cb2d69ad.html" data-snip="FIG-cfa12bb3cb2d69ad">SWS EcuM Fixed p. 32</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02684" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02684">[SWS_EcuM_02684]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02932" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02932">[SWS_EcuM_02932]</a></p>

<h4>UP phase: RUN/POST_RUN requests and mode switches</h4>
<p>If <code>EcuMModeHandling</code> is active <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04115" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04115">[SWS_EcuM_04115]</a>, configured users can request and release RUN and POST_RUN <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04130" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04130">[SWS_EcuM_04130]</a>. For this purpose, <code>EcuM_RequestRUN</code>, <code>EcuM_ReleaseRUN</code>, <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN</code>, and <code>EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN</code> are available <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04129" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04129">[SWS_EcuM_04129]</a>. The EcuM tracks the requests per user <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04126" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04126">[SWS_EcuM_04126]</a> and separately for RUN and POST_RUN (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_3_3_4_EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_3_3_4_EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN">SWS EcuM p. 116</a>). A user cannot place a request multiple times <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04125" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04125">[SWS_EcuM_04125]</a>.</p>
<p>The EcuM reports the arbitration result via <code>BswM_EcuM_RequestedState</code>:</p>
<ul>
<li>Upon the first request, it reports <code>ECUM_RUNSTATUS_REQUESTED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04144" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04144">[SWS_EcuM_04144]</a>.</li>
<li>Upon release of the last request, it reports <code>ECUM_RUNSTATUS_RELEASED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04117" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04117">[SWS_EcuM_04117]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04119" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04119">[SWS_EcuM_04119]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>Thereupon, BswM sets the new state with <code>EcuM_SetState</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04122">[SWS_EcuM_04122]</a>. The EcuM forwards the mode via the port <code>currentMode</code> to the RTE <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04133">[SWS_EcuM_04133]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>. Following feedback from the RTE, it reports the state to BswM with <code>BswM_EcuM_CurrentState</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04143">[SWS_EcuM_04143]</a>. Example rules for BswM are contained in the <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_3_3_1_3_Shutdown_and_Sleep.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_3_3_1_3_Shutdown_and_Sleep">Mode-Mgmt-Guide p. 34</a>.</p>
<p>As long as the OS is running, <code>EcuM_MainFunction</code> handles the ongoing tasks of the EcuM <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02837" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02837">[SWS_EcuM_02837]</a>. These include wakeup validation <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02539" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02539">[SWS_EcuM_02539]</a> and, if configured, the wakeup timer <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04002">[SWS_EcuM_04002]</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequence diagram: The EcuM collects the requests and reports only the arbitration result. BswM triggers the state transition; the RTE receives the mode only thereafter. Sources: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04144" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04144">[SWS_EcuM_04144]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04117" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04117">[SWS_EcuM_04117]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04116" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04116">[SWS_EcuM_04116]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04143">[SWS_EcuM_04143]</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_3_3_1_2_Running.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_MODEMANAGEMENTGUIDE_SECTION_3_3_1_2_Running">Mode-Mgmt-Guide p. 34</a></p>

<h4>Shutdown targets and shutdown to OFF or RESET</h4>
<p>Shutdown targets are states in which no code is executed: Off, Sleep, and Reset (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_7_Shutdown_Targets.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_7_Shutdown_Targets">SWS EcuM p. 66</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04136" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04136">[SWS_EcuM_04136]</a>). <code>EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget</code> merely stores the target and initiates nothing on its own <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02585" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02585">[SWS_EcuM_02585]</a>. The mode parameter applies only to SLEEP and RESET <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02979" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02979">[SWS_EcuM_02979]</a>. Available reset modalities are at least <code>Mcu_PerformReset</code>, <code>WdgM_PerformReset</code>, and toggling an I/O pin <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04005">[SWS_EcuM_04005]</a>. Additionally, a shutdown cause can be recorded <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04050" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04050">[SWS_EcuM_04050]</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">State diagram: The lifecycle passes through the phases STARTUP, UP, SLEEP, and SHUTDOWN. From SLEEP, a wakeup event leads back to UP, whereas a reset leads to STARTUP. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_FIGURE_Figure_7_17.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_FIGURE_Figure_7_17">SWS EcuM p. 71</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_STD_SECTION_7_5_SLEEP_Phase.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_STD_SECTION_7_5_SLEEP_Phase">SWS EcuM p. 54</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02963" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02963">[SWS_EcuM_02963]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04001">[SWS_EcuM_04001]</a></p>
<p>Entry into SHUTDOWN is controlled by BswM. It is likely to occur via <code>EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll</code> as well, since the synchronization diagram mentions this call by BswM (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_FIGURE_Figure_7_18.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_FIGURE_Figure_7_18">SWS EcuM p. 74</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91002">[SWS_EcuM_91002]</a>). The OffPreOS sequence calls <code>EcuM_OnGoOffOne</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02916" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02916">[SWS_EcuM_02916]</a> and deinitializes BswM and SchM (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_BSWM_SECTION_7_9_6_1_Master_Core_SHUTDOWN.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_BSWM_SECTION_7_9_6_1_Master_Core_SHUTDOWN">SWS EcuM p. 90</a>). As the last step, it calls <code>ShutdownOS</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02952" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02952">[SWS_EcuM_02952]</a>. If a wakeup event occurs during this process, the EcuM must terminate shutdown and restart immediately <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02756" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02756">[SWS_EcuM_02756]</a>. Presumably, this occurs by switching the target to RESET.</p>
<p>The shutdown hook calls <code>EcuM_Shutdown</code>, which does not return <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02953" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02953">[SWS_EcuM_02953]</a>. The OffPostOS sequence follows: <code>EcuM_OnGoOffTwo</code>, then depending on the target <code>EcuM_AL_Reset</code> or <code>EcuM_AL_SwitchOff</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04074" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04074">[SWS_EcuM_04074]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04075" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04075">[SWS_EcuM_04075]</a>. If the reset mode originates from a <code>EcuM_ShutdownModeType</code>, it must be shifted right by one byte prior to handover (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_5_3_4_EcuM_AL_Reset.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_5_3_4_EcuM_AL_Reset">SWS EcuM p. 142</a>).</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Activity diagram: Shutdown branches twice. First, OffPreOS checks for pending wakeup events; then, OffPostOS selects between RESET and OFF. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_4_2_Activities_in_the_OffPostOS_Sequence.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_4_2_Activities_in_the_OffPostOS_Sequence">SWS EcuM p. 50</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-5433a6dad4388f21.html" data-snip="FIG-5433a6dad4388f21">SWS EcuM p. 82</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02756" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02756">[SWS_EcuM_02756]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02953" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02953">[SWS_EcuM_02953]</a></p>

<h4>Sleep phase: GoSleep, Halt or Poll, WakeupRestart</h4>
<p><code>EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll</code> with target SLEEP first starts the GoSleep sequence. Thereafter, depending on <code>EcuMSleepModeSuspend</code>, the Halt or the Poll sequence follows (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_STD_SECTION_7_5_SLEEP_Phase.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_STD_SECTION_7_5_SLEEP_Phase">SWS EcuM p. 54</a>). The OS remains active in this phase <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02951" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02951">[SWS_EcuM_02951]</a>. GoSleep arms the wakeup sources configured for the sleep mode <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02389" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02389">[SWS_EcuM_02389]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02546" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02546">[SWS_EcuM_02546]</a> and allocates the resource <code>RES_AUTOSAR_ECUM</code> per core <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03010">[SWS_EcuM_03010]</a>. If a wakeup event occurs already during GoSleep, Halt and Poll must no longer be entered <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02188" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02188">[SWS_EcuM_02188]</a>.</p>
<p>The two sleep variants differ as follows:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Halt:</strong> The microcontroller is halted, no code is executed <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02960" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02960">[SWS_EcuM_02960]</a>. Beforehand, <code>EcuM_GenerateRamHash</code> calculates a checksum over the RAM; after waking up, <code>EcuM_CheckRamHash</code> verifies it. In case of multiple cores, this occurs only on the master <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02863" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02863">[SWS_EcuM_02863]</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Poll:</strong> The controller continues to execute code <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02962" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02962">[SWS_EcuM_02962]</a>. In R20-11, the EcuM calls <code>EcuM_SleepActivity</code> and the callout <code>EcuM_CheckWakeup</code> in a blocking loop until a wakeup event is present <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03020" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03020">[SWS_EcuM_03020]</a>. Starting with R21-11, this callout is named <code>EcuM_CheckWakeupHook</code>, and <code>EcuM_CheckWakeup</code> becomes an EcuM function (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_5_4_5_EcuM_CheckWakeupHook.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_5_4_5_EcuM_CheckWakeupHook">SWS EcuM p. 145</a>).</li>
</ul>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequence diagram: The Halt sequence surrounds standstill with generation and verification of the RAM checksum. Thereafter, it reports the wakeup source to BswM, as PENDING or VALIDATED. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-45500c46de851bae.html" data-snip="FIG-45500c46de851bae">SWS EcuM p. 85</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02863" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02863">[SWS_EcuM_02863]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02987" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02987">[SWS_EcuM_02987]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02963" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02963">[SWS_EcuM_02963]</a></p>
<p>Following a wakeup event, the EcuM regains control and executes the WakeupRestart sequence <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02963" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02963">[SWS_EcuM_02963]</a>. It encompasses:</p>
<ul>
<li>restoring MCU normal mode,</li>
<li>disabling pending wakeup sources <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04084" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04084">[SWS_EcuM_04084]</a>,</li>
<li>re-initializing drivers via <code>EcuM_AL_DriverRestart</code> and re-arming their wakeup callback <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02562" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02562">[SWS_EcuM_02562]</a>,</li>
<li>releasing the scheduler (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_5_5_Activities_in_the_WakeupRestart_Sequence.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_5_5_Activities_in_the_WakeupRestart_Sequence">SWS EcuM p. 56</a>).</li>
</ul>

<h4>Wakeup sources: bitmask, states, and validation protocol</h4>
<p>The EcuM manages up to 32 wakeup sources as bits in <code>EcuM_WakeupSourceType</code>. Five positions are predefined (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_6_3_Internal_Representation_of_Wakeup_States.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_6_3_Internal_Representation_of_Wakeup_States">SWS EcuM p. 63</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04040" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04040">[SWS_EcuM_04040]</a>). Further sources occupy bits 5 to 31 via <code>EcuMWakeupSourceId</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02165" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02165">[SWS_EcuM_02165]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02166" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02166">[SWS_EcuM_02166]</a>. Each source is in one of four states: NONE, PENDING, VALIDATED, or EXPIRED <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04091" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04091">[SWS_EcuM_04091]</a>. The EcuM reports every state change as a mode request to BswM <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04003">[SWS_EcuM_04003]</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">State diagram: A source without validation requirement transitions directly to VALIDATED. All others wait in PENDING for confirmation or time out into EXPIRED. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-407eea1386f12f08.html" data-snip="FIG-407eea1386f12f08">SWS EcuM p. 60</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04091" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04091">[SWS_EcuM_04091]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02566" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02566">[SWS_EcuM_02566]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02683" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02683">[SWS_EcuM_02683]</a></p>
<p>A driver reports a detected event once with <code>EcuM_SetWakeupEvent</code> (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_6_4_4_Requirements_for_Drivers_with_Wakeup_Sources.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_6_4_4_Requirements_for_Drivers_with_Wakeup_Sources">SWS EcuM p. 71</a>). This is permitted from interrupts as well <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02171" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02171">[SWS_EcuM_02171]</a>. The function sets the pending bit <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_01117" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_01117">[SWS_EcuM_01117]</a> and ignores sources that do not belong to the selected sleep mode <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04138" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04138">[SWS_EcuM_04138]</a>. In addition, it starts the validation timer, but not again upon repeated calls for the same source <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02709" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02709">[SWS_EcuM_02709]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02712" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02712">[SWS_EcuM_02712]</a>. If no validation is configured for a source, the event is considered validated immediately <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02566" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02566">[SWS_EcuM_02566]</a>. Reset and power sources are never validated <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02625" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02625">[SWS_EcuM_02625]</a>.</p>
<p>Validation runs in <code>EcuM_MainFunction</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02539" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02539">[SWS_EcuM_02539]</a> and follows this protocol:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>EcuM_StartWakeupSources</code> prepares the sources, <code>EcuM_CheckValidation</code> subsequently queries them <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02924" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02924">[SWS_EcuM_02924]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02925" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02925">[SWS_EcuM_02925]</a>.</li>
<li>If validation succeeds, the validating module calls <code>EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent</code>. The EcuM then stops the timer, sets the validated bit, reports VALIDATED to BswM, and informs ComM <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04078" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04078">[SWS_EcuM_04078]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02710" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02710">[SWS_EcuM_02710]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04079" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04079">[SWS_EcuM_04079]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02645" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02645">[SWS_EcuM_02645]</a>.</li>
<li>If the timer expires, the EcuM sets the expired bit, reports EXPIRED to BswM, and calls <code>EcuM_StopWakeupSources</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04081" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04081">[SWS_EcuM_04081]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04082" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04082">[SWS_EcuM_04082]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02926" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02926">[SWS_EcuM_02926]</a>.</li>
<li>In the RUN state, validation is effective only for communication channels <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02790" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02790">[SWS_EcuM_02790]</a>.</li>
<li><code>EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent</code> clears the bits in all three internal variables <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02683" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02683">[SWS_EcuM_02683]</a>.</li>
<li>A running CheckWakeupTimer prevents shutdown before a source has been checked <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04096" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04096">[SWS_EcuM_04096]</a>. <code>EcuM_SetWakeupEvent</code> cancels it <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04098" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04098">[SWS_EcuM_04098]</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p class="diagram-note">Sequence diagram: Validation is a loop with two outcomes: confirmation or timeout. Each outcome generates its own reports to BswM and ComM. Sources: <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/figures/FIG-70879b6d276c3179.html" data-snip="FIG-70879b6d276c3179">SWS EcuM p. 63</a>, <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_COMM_SECTION_7_6_4_Activities_in_the_WakeupValidation_Sequence.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_COMM_SECTION_7_6_4_Activities_in_the_WakeupValidation_Sequence">SWS EcuM p. 64</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02709" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02709">[SWS_EcuM_02709]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04082" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04082">[SWS_EcuM_04082]</a></p>

<h4>Multicore operation, wakeup timer, and boot target</h4>
<p>On multicore ECUs, one EcuM instance runs per core. The master EcuM starts the remaining cores (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_FIGURE_Figure_7_17.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_FIGURE_Figure_7_17">SWS EcuM p. 71</a>). For each instance:</p>
<ul>
<li>The init callouts initialize only the MCAL modules of their own core <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04145" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04145">[SWS_EcuM_04145]</a>.</li>
<li>OS and SchM are started on each core <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04093" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04093">[SWS_EcuM_04093]</a>.</li>
<li>Each instance processes the wakeup events of its core <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04012">[SWS_EcuM_04012]</a>.</li>
<li>The SLEEP target puts all cores to sleep <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04092" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04092">[SWS_EcuM_04092]</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p>The optional wakeup timer counts seconds since the battery was connected <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04069" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04069">[SWS_EcuM_04069]</a>. Each user has at most one alarm <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04070" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04070">[SWS_EcuM_04070]</a>, and the master alarm follows the earliest user alarm <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04072" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04072">[SWS_EcuM_04072]</a>. A later alarm returns <code>ECUM_E_EARLIER_ACTIVE</code>, a past point in time <code>ECUM_E_PAST</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04059" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04059">[SWS_EcuM_04059]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04060" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04060">[SWS_EcuM_04060]</a>. When alarms are cleared is governed by <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04010">[SWS_EcuM_04010]</a>. <code>EcuM_SelectBootTarget</code> stores the boot target so that the bootloader can read it <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02247" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02247">[SWS_EcuM_02247]</a>.</p>

<h4>Behavior in the event of an error</h4>
<p><strong>Unrecoverable errors:</strong> Here, the EcuM calls <code>EcuM_ErrorHook</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04033" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04033">[SWS_EcuM_04033]</a>, specifically with <code>ECUM_E_CONFIGURATION_DATA_INCONSISTENT</code> or <code>ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_FAILED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91003" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91003">[SWS_EcuM_91003]</a> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02987" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02987">[SWS_EcuM_02987]</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Failed OS calls:</strong> According to R20-11, the state remains unchanged, and the EcuM reports the error via the ErrorHook <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04139" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04139">[SWS_EcuM_04139]</a>. The dedicated code <code>ECUM_E_OS_CALL_FAILED</code> and the assumption that the hook does not return are first mentioned in a later release (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_12_ErrorHook.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_12_ErrorHook">SWS EcuM p. 102</a>).</p>
<p><strong>Further rules:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>The EcuM ignores errors during initialization <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02980" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02980">[SWS_EcuM_02980]</a>.</li>
<li>It maps an unknown reset reason to <code>ECUM_WKSOURCE_RESET</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02601" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02601">[SWS_EcuM_02601]</a>.</li>
<li>A reset or power cycle during Halt or Poll leads back to STARTUP <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04001">[SWS_EcuM_04001]</a>.</li>
<li>If the ECU cannot de-energize itself in <code>EcuM_AL_SwitchOff</code>, a reset is the appropriate reaction. The integrator is permitted to limit the endless loop (<a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_5_3_3_EcuM_AL_SwitchOff.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_8_5_3_3_EcuM_AL_SwitchOff">SWS EcuM p. 141</a>).</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Development errors to the DET:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>general codes <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03009">[SWS_EcuM_03009]</a>,</li>
<li>multiple requests <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03024" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03024">[SWS_EcuM_03024]</a> and releases without request <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03023" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03023">[SWS_EcuM_03023]</a>,</li>
<li>unknown wakeup sources <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02867" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02867">[SWS_EcuM_02867]</a>,</li>
<li>invalid states in <code>EcuM_SetState</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04123" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04123">[SWS_EcuM_04123]</a>.</li>
</ul>

<h4>Further detailed evidence</h4>
<ul>
<li>Startup: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02411" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02411">[SWS_EcuM_02411]</a> (StartPreOS in <code>EcuM_Init</code>), <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02795" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02795">[SWS_EcuM_02795]</a> (consistency hash), <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_3_5_Driver_Initialization.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_3_5_Driver_Initialization">SWS EcuM p. 46</a> (driver initialization).</li>
<li>Mode handling: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04120" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04120">[SWS_EcuM_04120]</a> (<code>EcuM_RunStatusType</code>), <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a> (<code>EcuM_StateType</code>).</li>
<li>Shutdown: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02156" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02156">[SWS_EcuM_02156]</a> (last shutdown target), <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04007" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04007">[SWS_EcuM_04007]</a> (shutdown causes).</li>
<li>Sleep and wakeup: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04066" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04066">[SWS_EcuM_04066]</a> (WakeupRestart), <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02947" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02947">[SWS_EcuM_02947]</a> (restart list), <a class="docref internal-spec-ref" href="../../../spec/snippets/SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_6_7_Wakeup_Sources_with_Integrated_Power_Control.html" data-snip="SNIP_CLASSIC_ECUM_SECTION_7_6_7_Wakeup_Sources_with_Integrated_Power_Control">SWS EcuM p. 70</a> (SLEEP via system module).</li>
<li>Multicore: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04015" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04015">[SWS_EcuM_04015]</a> to <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04030" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04030">[SWS_EcuM_04030]</a> (master/slave sequences).</li>
</ul>
